title: AWS Collector Output
description: Security posture output from the epack AWS collector. The `collected_at_level` field indicates how much detail this artifact contains. Level-gated arrays are absent below their level, `[]` when collected with no rows, and `[...]` when populated. A value the collector could not read is null, and the run's result says why. See docs/levels.md for the artifact contract.

schema_version.description: Version of this schema the artifact follows. Always 1.0.0 in v1.
schema_version.x-epack-summary: Version of the schema this artifact follows, which is always 1.0.0 in v1.

collected_at.description: When the collection ran, in RFC 3339.
collected_at.x-epack-summary: When the collection ran, in UTC.

collected_at_level.description: Collection level the artifact was produced at. See docs/levels.md.

accounts.description: One entry for each account the collector signed in to, in the order the configuration lists them.
accounts.x-epack-summary: One posture record per AWS account that was scanned.

items.x-epack-summary: Security posture for one AWS account.

failed_accounts.description: Configured accounts whose collection failed entirely, so no entry exists for them under accounts. Absent when every account answered.
failed_accounts.x-epack-summary: Configured accounts the collector could not sign in to, so they have no entry under Accounts. When every configured account fails, the run fails and no artifact is written.
failed_accounts.x-epack-method: Lists a configured account when the collector cannot sign in to it, meaning its AWS client could not be created or STS GetCallerIdentity with the configured role failed.

account_id.description: Parsed from the configured role ARN; absent when not derivable (e.g. default credentials).
account_id.x-epack-summary: The failed account's 12-digit number, parsed from its configured role. Absent when it could not be derived.

role_arn.description: The role the account's configuration entry names, when it names one.
role_arn.x-epack-summary: The role the collector was configured to assume for this account.

label.description: Operator-supplied label from the account's config entry.
label.x-epack-summary: Label your team assigned to this account in the collector configuration, so a failed account is identifiable by environment.

error_code.description: AWS's error code for the failure that stopped the account's collection, such as AccessDenied, or NonAPIError when AWS sent none.
error_code.x-epack-summary: Why collection failed for this account, such as a denied role assumption.

diagnostics.description: Per-account errors and surface-level warnings encountered during collection. Absent when there were none.
diagnostics.x-epack-summary: Errors and warnings from the collection, such as a service call that was denied.

account_errors.description: One message for each configured account whose collection failed entirely.
account_errors.x-epack-summary: One message for each configured account whose collection failed entirely. Those accounts have no entry under Accounts.

warnings.description: Messages about reads that failed, were cut short, or met an unexpected answer. The run's result lists each value left out and why.
warnings.x-epack-summary: Messages about reads that failed or were cut short, such as a denied service call. A value may be missing or incomplete because of one of these.

AccountPosture.description: The security posture of one AWS account.

account_id.x-epack-summary: The 12-digit AWS account number this record covers.

account_alias.description: The account's IAM alias. Absent when the account has none.
account_alias.x-epack-summary: Friendly alias set on the account, if any. Absent when no alias is configured.

account_label.description: Operator-supplied label from the account's config entry (e.g. production, staging), passed through verbatim. Absent when not configured.
account_label.x-epack-summary: Label your team assigned to this account in the collector configuration, such as production or staging. Absent when none was configured.

regions.description: The regions scanned: the configured list, or every region the account has enabled.
regions.x-epack-summary: AWS regions this scan covered. Regional services (such as GuardDuty or KMS) are only assessed in these regions.

iam.description: IAM users, their credentials, the password policy, the root user, and roles.
iam.x-epack-summary: How IAM users and the root user are protected. At audit level and above it also lists the account's roles and who outside the account can assume them.

s3.description: S3 buckets: public access blocks, encryption, versioning, logging, and transport enforcement.
s3.x-epack-summary: How well stored files are protected from public exposure and loss.

rds.description: RDS databases across the scanned regions.
rds.x-epack-summary: Protection settings across managed relational databases.

network.description: VPCs and security group exposure across the scanned regions.
network.x-epack-summary: VPCs and security groups across the scanned regions, with which groups open SSH or RDP to any address.

account_security.description: The account's security services: CloudTrail, AWS Config, GuardDuty, IAM Access Analyzer, Security Hub, and Inspector.
account_security.x-epack-summary: Whether the account's security logging and threat detection services are turned on.

identity_center.description: IAM Identity Center, looked for in every scanned region.
identity_center.x-epack-summary: Workforce users sign in through IAM Identity Center, formerly AWS SSO, to reach the organization's AWS accounts. The collector looks for an instance in every scanned region.

lambda.description: Lambda functions across the scanned regions.
lambda.x-epack-summary: Lambda functions across the scanned regions, including any on deprecated runtimes or with public function URLs.

ec2.description: EC2 instances and EBS volumes across the scanned regions.
ec2.x-epack-summary: EC2 instances and EBS volumes across the scanned regions, with the settings that expose instances or their data.

cloudwatch_logs.description: CloudWatch log groups across the scanned regions.
cloudwatch_logs.x-epack-summary: Retention and encryption settings of CloudWatch log groups across the scanned regions. No log content is collected.

monitoring.description: CloudWatch alarms across the scanned regions, and whether their notifications reach anyone.
monitoring.x-epack-summary: CloudWatch metric alarms and whether their notifications reach a confirmed subscriber. Alerts routed through EventBridge or a third-party monitor are not covered, so zero alarms does not mean nobody is paged.

stored_images.description: EBS snapshots and AMIs the account owns, across the scanned regions.
stored_images.x-epack-summary: EBS snapshots and AMIs this account owns, and whether each is public or unencrypted. Snapshots and images owned by other accounts are not listed.

load_balancers.description: Elastic Load Balancing load balancers and target groups across the scanned regions.
load_balancers.x-epack-summary: Whether each load balancer forces TLS or accepts plaintext, read from its listener settings. Also covers zone redundancy and target group health checks.

cloudfront.x-epack-summary: Whether CloudFront distributions use TLS from viewers to the edge and from the edge to origins. The values come from each distribution's settings.

ses.description: SES configuration sets and sending identities across the scanned regions.
ses.x-epack-summary: Whether outbound mail must travel over TLS. SES falls back to plaintext unless the configuration set used for a send has a TLS policy of REQUIRE.

ecs.description: ECS services across the scanned regions.
ecs.x-epack-summary: How ECS services scale and whether a failing deployment stops automatically. Task definitions are never read, because their environment variables often hold credentials.

auto_scaling.description: EC2 Auto Scaling groups across the scanned regions.
auto_scaling.x-epack-summary: How EC2 Auto Scaling groups scale and whether they replace unhealthy instances.

waf.description: WAF web ACLs across the scanned regions and the CloudFront scope.
waf.x-epack-summary: Whether internet-facing entry points have a web application firewall attached, and whether request-rate limiting is enforced.

kms.description: Customer managed KMS keys across the scanned regions.
kms.x-epack-summary: Customer managed KMS keys across the scanned regions. AWS managed keys are left out because the account cannot change their rotation or key policy.

secrets_manager.description: Secrets Manager secrets across the scanned regions.
secrets_manager.x-epack-summary: Secrets Manager secrets across the scanned regions. Secret values are not collected.

ssm_parameters.description: Systems Manager Parameter Store parameters across the scanned regions.
ssm_parameters.x-epack-summary: Parameter Store parameters across the scanned regions. Parameter values are not collected.

IAMMetrics.description: IAM in the account. The user figures come from the IAM credential report, the root user excluded.

credential_report_evaluated.description: True when the IAM credential report was collected. The user aggregates (iam_users_present, mfa_enabled, hardware_mfa_enabled, access_keys_rotated) are meaningful only when true; on collection failure they are null.
credential_report_evaluated.x-epack-summary: Whether the IAM credential report was read. When it wasn't, the IAM user counts and percentages are left out.
credential_report_evaluated.x-epack-method: Records whether GetCredentialReport returned a report within 45 seconds of polling after GenerateCredentialReport.

credential_report_error_code.description: Present when the credential report was not evaluated (e.g. CredentialReportTimeout).
credential_report_error_code.x-epack-summary: Why the credential report could not be read, such as a generation timeout. Present only when it was not evaluated.

iam_users_present.description: Whether the credential report lists any IAM user besides the root user.
iam_users_present.x-epack-summary: Whether the account has any IAM user besides the root user. People who sign in through Identity Center or a SAML provider are not IAM users.
iam_users_present.x-epack-method: Sets true when the GetCredentialReport report has a row other than <root_account>.

iam_user_count.description: IAM users in the credential report, the root user excluded.
iam_user_count.x-epack-summary: Number of IAM users in the credential report, excluding the root user. The user MFA percentages are shares of this number, so an account with none has no MFA percentage.
iam_user_count.x-epack-method: Counts the GetCredentialReport rows other than <root_account>.

access_key_user_count.description: IAM users with at least one active access key.
access_key_user_count.x-epack-summary: Number of IAM users with at least one active access key. Key rotation is measured over these users, so an account where no user has a key has no rotation percentage.
access_key_user_count.x-epack-method: Counts the non-root credential report rows where access_key_1_active or access_key_2_active is true.

password_policy_evaluated.description: True when the account password policy was read, whether or not one is configured. False means the lookup failed; see password_policy_error_code.
password_policy_evaluated.x-epack-summary: Whether the account password policy was read, including when none is configured. When the read failed, the policy and its settings are left out.
password_policy_evaluated.x-epack-method: Records whether GetAccountPasswordPolicy succeeded, counting a NoSuchEntity error as a read that found no policy.

password_policy_error_code.description: Why the account password policy could not be read.
password_policy_error_code.x-epack-summary: Why the account password policy could not be read, when applicable.

password_policy.description: The configured account password policy for IAM console sign-in. Null while password_policy_evaluated is true means no policy is configured and AWS's own default applies, which is a finding rather than missing data.
password_policy.x-epack-summary: The account's rules for IAM console passwords. Absent after a successful read means no policy is set, so AWS's default policy applies to IAM user passwords.

minimum_length.description: Shortest console password the account accepts.
minimum_length.x-epack-summary: Shortest console password the account accepts.

require_symbols.description: Whether passwords must contain a symbol.
require_symbols.x-epack-summary: Whether a console password must contain a symbol.

require_numbers.description: Whether passwords must contain a number.
require_numbers.x-epack-summary: Whether a console password must contain a number.

require_uppercase.description: Whether passwords must contain an uppercase letter.
require_uppercase.x-epack-summary: Whether a console password must contain an uppercase letter.

require_lowercase.description: Whether passwords must contain a lowercase letter.
require_lowercase.x-epack-summary: Whether a console password must contain a lowercase letter.

allow_users_to_change_password.description: Whether IAM users can change their own passwords.
allow_users_to_change_password.x-epack-summary: Whether users can rotate their own console password without an administrator.

expire_passwords.x-epack-summary: Whether console passwords expire after the number of days in Password expiry.

hard_expiry.description: Whether users are locked out rather than prompted once a password expires.
hard_expiry.x-epack-summary: Whether a user with an expired console password must have an administrator reset it. When false, the user sets a new password at sign-in.
hard_expiry.x-epack-method: Reads HardExpiry from GetAccountPasswordPolicy and treats a missing value as false.

max_password_age_days.description: Absent means passwords do not expire.
max_password_age_days.x-epack-summary: Days before a console password must be changed. Absent means passwords never expire.
max_password_age_days.x-epack-method: Reads MaxPasswordAge from GetAccountPasswordPolicy and leaves it out when it is missing or zero.

password_reuse_prevention.description: Absent means previous passwords may be reused.
password_reuse_prevention.x-epack-summary: How many previous passwords cannot be reused. Absent means a previous password may be set again.
password_reuse_prevention.x-epack-method: Reads PasswordReusePrevention from GetAccountPasswordPolicy and leaves it out when it is missing or zero.

password_policy.x-epack-null: No account password policy is configured, so AWS's default applies

mfa_enabled.description: Percentage of IAM users with an MFA device active. Null when there are no IAM users.
mfa_enabled.x-epack-summary: Share of IAM users with an MFA device active, and absent when the account has no IAM users. People who sign in through Identity Center are not IAM users and are not counted.
mfa_enabled.x-epack-method: Divides mfa_enabled_user_count by iam_user_count and rounds down.

mfa_enabled_user_count.description: IAM users with an MFA device active.
mfa_enabled_user_count.x-epack-summary: Number of IAM users with an MFA device active. Divided by IAM users and rounded down, it gives the Users with MFA percentage.
mfa_enabled_user_count.x-epack-method: Counts the non-root credential report rows whose mfa_active is true.

hardware_mfa_enabled.description: Percentage of IAM users with a hardware MFA device, a FIDO security key or a hardware TOTP token rather than a virtual device. Null when there are no IAM users.
hardware_mfa_enabled.x-epack-summary: Share of IAM users with a FIDO security key or a hardware TOTP token. Absent when the account has no IAM users or any user's MFA devices could not be listed.
hardware_mfa_enabled.x-epack-method: Divides hardware_mfa_enabled_user_count by iam_user_count and rounds down.

hardware_mfa_enabled_user_count.description: IAM users with a hardware MFA device: a FIDO security key or a hardware TOTP token rather than a virtual device.
hardware_mfa_enabled_user_count.x-epack-summary: Number of IAM users with a hardware MFA device, such as a FIDO security key or a hardware token. Divided by IAM users and rounded down, it gives the Users with hardware MFA percentage.
hardware_mfa_enabled_user_count.x-epack-method: Calls ListMFADevices for each IAM user with MFA active and counts the users with a device whose serial number is neither a virtual :mfa/ ARN nor an SMS :sms-mfa/ ARN.

access_keys_rotated.description: Percentage of IAM users with an active access key whose every active key was created or rotated in the last 90 days. Null when no user has an active key.
access_keys_rotated.x-epack-summary: Share of IAM users with an active access key whose every active key was created or rotated in the last 90 days. Absent when no user has an active key.
access_keys_rotated.x-epack-method: Divides access_keys_rotated_user_count by access_key_user_count and rounds down.

access_keys_rotated_user_count.description: IAM users with an active access key whose every active key was created or rotated in the last 90 days.
access_keys_rotated_user_count.x-epack-summary: Number of users whose every active access key was created or rotated in the last 90 days. Divided by IAM users with access keys and rounded down, it gives the Keys rotated in 90 days percentage.
access_keys_rotated_user_count.x-epack-method: Counts the users with an active access key whose every active key has a last rotated date in the credential report within 90 days of the run.

saml_provider_count.description: SAML identity providers the account trusts for sign-in. The ones IAM Identity Center creates, whose names start with AWSSSO_, are counted in identity_center_saml_provider_count instead.
saml_provider_count.x-epack-summary: SAML identity providers the account trusts for sign-in, leaving out the ones IAM Identity Center creates. People who sign in through one aren't IAM users, so the user MFA percentages don't cover them.
saml_provider_count.x-epack-method: Calls ListSAMLProviders and counts the providers whose names don't start with AWSSSO_.

identity_center_saml_provider_count.description: SAML providers IAM Identity Center created in the account, whose names start with AWSSSO_.
identity_center_saml_provider_count.x-epack-summary: SAML providers IAM Identity Center created in the account, whose names start with AWSSSO_. When the account has one, people can sign in to it through Identity Center.
identity_center_saml_provider_count.x-epack-method: Calls ListSAMLProviders and counts the providers whose names start with AWSSSO_.

identity_center_role_count.description: Roles IAM Identity Center provisioned in the account for its permission sets, under the /aws-reserved/sso.amazonaws.com/ path and named AWSReservedSSO_. A member account has them even though it cannot see its organization's Identity Center instance.
identity_center_role_count.x-epack-summary: Roles IAM Identity Center provisioned in the account for its permission sets, whose names start with AWSReservedSSO_. A member account has them even though it can't see its organization's Identity Center instance.
identity_center_role_count.x-epack-method: Calls ListRoles with the path prefix /aws-reserved/sso.amazonaws.com/ and counts the roles whose names start with AWSReservedSSO_.

root_credential_state_evaluated.description: True when root credential state was read from the credential report or the account summary. The root_* credential flags are meaningful only when true.
root_credential_state_evaluated.x-epack-summary: Whether the root user's credential state was read from the account summary or the credential report. The root flags are meaningful only when this is true.
root_credential_state_evaluated.x-epack-method: Records whether GetAccountSummary succeeded or, when it failed, whether the credential report had a <root_account> row.

root_mfa_enabled.description: True when root MFA is active.
root_mfa_enabled.x-epack-summary: Whether the root user has MFA active. An account with no root credentials reads false here and true under Root access protected.
root_mfa_enabled.x-epack-method: Reads AccountMFAEnabled from GetAccountSummary, or mfa_active on the credential report's <root_account> row when that call fails.

root_credentials_present.description: Whether the root user has a password, an access key, or a signing certificate.
root_credentials_present.x-epack-summary: Whether the root user has a password, an access key or a signing certificate. An organization can remove them through centralized root credentials management.
root_credentials_present.x-epack-method: Sets true when GetAccountSummary shows a root password, access key or signing certificate, and falls back to the credential report's root key and certificate columns when that call fails.

root_password_present.description: Whether the root user has a password. The credential report alone cannot tell, so it comes from the account summary.
root_password_present.x-epack-summary: Whether the root user has a console password. It is left out when only the credential report was read, since the report's root row has no password value.

root_access_keys_exist.description: Whether the root user has an access key.
root_access_keys_exist.x-epack-summary: Whether the root user has an access key. AWS advises deleting root access keys.
root_access_keys_exist.x-epack-method: Reads AccountAccessKeysPresent from GetAccountSummary, or the root row's access_key_1_active and access_key_2_active in the credential report when that call fails. Those columns are false for an inactive key too, so a false from the report is left out.

root_signing_certificates_present.description: Whether the root user has an X.509 signing certificate.
root_signing_certificates_present.x-epack-summary: Whether the root user has an X.509 signing certificate, a legacy long-term credential.
root_signing_certificates_present.x-epack-method: Reads AccountSigningCertificatesPresent from GetAccountSummary, or the root row's cert_1_active and cert_2_active in the credential report when that call fails. Those columns are false for an inactive certificate too, so a false from the report is left out.

root_access_protected.description: True when root MFA is active or no long-term root credentials are present.
root_access_protected.x-epack-summary: Whether the root user has MFA active or has no long-term credentials.
root_access_protected.x-epack-method: Sets true when root_mfa_enabled is true or root_credentials_present is false.

root_organizations_features_evaluated.description: True when IAM's centralized root access features were read. root_organization_id and the two feature flags are meaningful only when true.
root_organizations_features_evaluated.x-epack-summary: Whether the organization's centralized root access settings were read. It is false from a member account, which can't read them.

root_organization_id.description: The AWS Organizations ID that IAM's centralized root access features report.
root_organization_id.x-epack-summary: The AWS Organizations ID read with the centralized root access settings.

root_credentials_management_feature_enab.description: True when IAM ListOrganizationsFeatures reported the RootCredentialsManagement centralized root access feature.
root_credentials_management_feature_enab.x-epack-summary: Whether the organization has centralized root credentials management turned on, which lets it remove root credentials from member accounts. It can be read only from the management account or a delegated administrator.
root_credentials_management_feature_enab.x-epack-method: Calls IAM ListOrganizationsFeatures and checks EnabledFeatures for RootCredentialsManagement.

root_sessions_feature_enabled.description: True when IAM ListOrganizationsFeatures reported the RootSessions centralized root access feature.
root_sessions_feature_enabled.x-epack-summary: Whether the organization has centralized root sessions turned on, which lets it run short-lived root tasks in member accounts. It can be read only from the management account or a delegated administrator.
root_sessions_feature_enabled.x-epack-method: Calls IAM ListOrganizationsFeatures and checks EnabledFeatures for RootSessions.

root_organizations_features_error_code.description: Present when the centralized root access feature read was not evaluated.
root_organizations_features_error_code.x-epack-summary: Why the centralized root access settings could not be read. From a member account this is an expected access error.

organization_accounts_evaluated.description: True when the AWS Organizations account roster was listed. Per-role external_trust_in_org determinations are meaningful only when true; member accounts without Organizations visibility record the error code without a warning.
organization_accounts_evaluated.x-epack-summary: Whether the organization's account list was read to check whether roles trust accounts inside the organization. It is read at audit level and above, and false is routine in a member account.
organization_accounts_evaluated.x-epack-method: Records whether AWS Organizations ListAccounts succeeded, counting AWSOrganizationsNotInUseException as a read that found no organization.

organization_accounts_error_code.description: Present when the organization account roster was not evaluated.
organization_accounts_error_code.x-epack-summary: Why the organization account list could not be read, when applicable.

users.description: Audit level and above: one row per IAM user in the credential report, the root user excluded.
users.x-epack-summary: Per-user rows the sign-in percentages were computed from. Empty list means no IAM users, absent means not collected.

roles.description: Audit level and above: one row per IAM role, with what its trust policy allows from outside the account.
roles.x-epack-summary: One row per IAM role, with what its trust policy allows from outside the account. It is absent when the role listing failed, and empty when the account has no roles.

credential_report.description: Internal level only: the IAM credential report the user figures come from, with each user's sign-in and access key activity.
credential_report.x-epack-summary: The IAM credential report the user figures come from, with each user's sign-in and access key activity. Collected only at the internal level.

generated_at.description: When AWS generated the report, in RFC 3339.
generated_at.x-epack-summary: When AWS generated this credential report. Reports can lag account state by up to four hours.

users.description: One row per user in the report, the root user included.
users.x-epack-summary: One row per principal. The root account appears as '<root_account>', matching AWS's own naming.

bucket_listing_evaluated.description: True when the bucket listing was collected. The bucket aggregates below are meaningful only when true; on listing failure they are null.
bucket_listing_evaluated.x-epack-summary: Whether the bucket listing was collected. When false, the bucket counts and percentages are left out.
bucket_listing_evaluated.x-epack-method: Records whether the ListBuckets call succeeded.

bucket_listing_error_code.description: Present when the bucket listing was not evaluated.
bucket_listing_error_code.x-epack-summary: Why the bucket listing could not be read, when applicable.

account_public_access_block_evaluated.description: True when the account-level S3 Block Public Access settings were read. account_public_access_block_enabled is meaningful only when true.
account_public_access_block_evaluated.x-epack-summary: Whether the account-wide public access block setting could be read. The account-wide flag below is meaningful only when this is true.
account_public_access_block_evaluated.x-epack-method: Records whether the S3 Control GetPublicAccessBlock call for the account succeeded, treating NoSuchPublicAccessBlockConfiguration as read with every flag off.

bucket_count.description: Total S3 buckets returned by ListBuckets.
bucket_count.x-epack-method: Counts the buckets that ListBuckets returns.

tls_enforced_bucket_count.description: Buckets whose policy conclusively denies plaintext access for every principal, every S3 action, and the whole bucket.
tls_enforced_bucket_count.x-epack-summary: Buckets whose policy denies every plaintext request to the bucket and its objects. S3 endpoints accept HTTP as well as HTTPS, so without such a deny, plaintext requests can reach the bucket.
tls_enforced_bucket_count.x-epack-method: Counts the buckets whose GetBucketPolicy document has a Deny on aws:SecureTransport false that covers every request to the bucket.

tls_enforcement_partial_bucket_count.description: Buckets with a transport deny that does not conclusively cover the whole bucket: scoped principals, subset actions, extra conditions, or partial resources.
tls_enforcement_partial_bucket_count.x-epack-summary: Buckets whose policy denies only some plaintext requests, such as those from certain callers or for certain objects. Plaintext requests outside the deny can still reach the bucket.
tls_enforcement_partial_bucket_count.x-epack-method: Counts the buckets whose GetBucketPolicy document has a Deny on aws:SecureTransport false that does not cover every request to the bucket.

tls_unenforced_bucket_count.description: Buckets whose policy says nothing about transport, or that have no policy. S3 endpoints answer HTTP, so plaintext requests are allowed.
tls_unenforced_bucket_count.x-epack-summary: Buckets with no policy, or with a policy that has no deny on insecure transport. Plaintext requests are allowed.
tls_unenforced_bucket_count.x-epack-method: Counts the buckets with no bucket policy, or whose GetBucketPolicy document has no Deny on aws:SecureTransport false.

tls_enforcement_unknown_bucket_count.description: Buckets whose policy could not be read. Unknown is never reported as unenforced.
tls_enforcement_unknown_bucket_count.x-epack-summary: Buckets whose policy could not be read, so their TLS enforcement is unknown. When this is above zero, the other TLS enforcement counts are left out.
tls_enforcement_unknown_bucket_count.x-epack-method: Counts the buckets whose GetBucketPolicy call failed or returned a policy that could not be parsed.

public_access_blocked.description: Percentage of buckets whose effective S3 Block Public Access settings block public access.
public_access_blocked.x-epack-summary: Share of buckets that block public access once account and bucket settings are combined. A bucket without the full block can be made public by its policy or ACL.
public_access_blocked.x-epack-method: Divides public_access_blocked_bucket_count by bucket_count and rounds down.

public_access_blocked_bucket_count.description: Buckets whose effective S3 Block Public Access settings block public access: each of the four flags set by the account or by the bucket.
public_access_blocked_bucket_count.x-epack-summary: Number of buckets with all four Block Public Access flags on, counting flags set at the account or the bucket. Divided by the bucket count and rounded down, it gives the Buckets blocking public access percentage.
public_access_blocked_bucket_count.x-epack-method: Counts the buckets where each of the four Block Public Access flags is on in either the account or the bucket GetPublicAccessBlock settings.

public_access_block_unknown_count.description: Buckets whose effective S3 Block Public Access setting could not be fully evaluated.
public_access_block_unknown_count.x-epack-summary: Buckets whose effective Block Public Access setting could not be fully read. When this is above zero, the public access percentage and count are left out.
public_access_block_unknown_count.x-epack-method: Counts the buckets that are not fully blocked by the settings that were read and whose account or bucket GetPublicAccessBlock call failed.

default_encryption_enabled.description: Percentage of buckets whose default encryption was evaluated and enabled.
default_encryption_enabled.x-epack-summary: Share of buckets that encrypt new objects by default, which S3 does for every bucket with SSE-S3. Buckets count here whether or not they use a KMS key.
default_encryption_enabled.x-epack-method: Divides default_encryption_enabled_bucket_count by bucket_count and rounds down.

default_encryption_enabled_bucket_count.description: Buckets whose default encryption was evaluated and enabled.
default_encryption_enabled_bucket_count.x-epack-summary: Number of buckets with default encryption on, counting buckets that rely on S3's SSE-S3 baseline. Divided by the bucket count and rounded down, it gives the Buckets encrypted by default percentage.
default_encryption_enabled_bucket_count.x-epack-method: Counts the buckets whose GetBucketEncryption call returned at least one rule or ServerSideEncryptionConfigurationNotFoundError.

default_encryption_evaluated_count.description: Buckets whose default encryption was read, or inferred from S3's SSE-S3 baseline when the bucket has no rule of its own.
default_encryption_evaluated_count.x-epack-summary: Buckets whose default encryption was read, or inferred from S3's SSE-S3 baseline when the bucket has no rule of its own.
default_encryption_evaluated_count.x-epack-method: Counts the buckets whose GetBucketEncryption call returned at least one rule or ServerSideEncryptionConfigurationNotFoundError.

default_encryption_inferred_count.description: Evaluated buckets counted as encrypted from documented AWS SSE-S3 baseline behavior rather than a readable encryption rule.
default_encryption_inferred_count.x-epack-summary: Buckets with no encryption rule of their own, counted as encrypted because S3 applies SSE-S3 to every bucket.
default_encryption_inferred_count.x-epack-method: Counts the buckets whose GetBucketEncryption call returned ServerSideEncryptionConfigurationNotFoundError.

default_encryption_unknown_count.description: Buckets whose default encryption could not be read.
default_encryption_unknown_count.x-epack-summary: Buckets whose default encryption could not be read. When this is above zero, the default encryption percentage and count are left out.
default_encryption_unknown_count.x-epack-method: Counts the buckets whose GetBucketEncryption call failed or returned no rules.

versioning_enabled.description: Percentage of buckets with versioning enabled. Null when there are no buckets.
versioning_enabled.x-epack-summary: Share of buckets that keep prior versions of objects. Versioning aids recovery from accidental deletes and ransomware.
versioning_enabled.x-epack-method: Divides versioning_enabled_bucket_count by bucket_count and rounds down.

versioning_enabled_bucket_count.x-epack-summary: Number of buckets with versioning on. Divided by the bucket count and rounded down, it gives the Buckets with versioning percentage.
versioning_enabled_bucket_count.x-epack-method: Counts the buckets whose GetBucketVersioning status is Enabled.

logging_enabled.description: Percentage of buckets with server access logging enabled. Log sink buckets (targets of other buckets' logging) are excluded from the denominator.
logging_enabled.x-epack-summary: Share of buckets that record who accessed them, not counting buckets that receive other buckets' access logs. Access logs support after-the-fact investigation.
logging_enabled.x-epack-method: Divides logging_enabled_bucket_count by logging_required_bucket_count and rounds down.

logging_enabled_bucket_count.description: Buckets that are not a server access log destination and have server access logging enabled.
logging_enabled_bucket_count.x-epack-summary: Buckets with server access logging on, leaving out log destination buckets. The access logging percentage divides this by the buckets that should log access.
logging_enabled_bucket_count.x-epack-method: Counts the buckets that are not a log destination and whose GetBucketLogging response has LoggingEnabled set.

log_sink_bucket_count.description: Buckets identified as server access log destinations for at least one other bucket. These are excluded from the logging_enabled denominator.
log_sink_bucket_count.x-epack-summary: Number of buckets that receive other buckets' server access logs. They are left out of the access logging percentage.
log_sink_bucket_count.x-epack-method: Counts the buckets named as the TargetBucket in another bucket's GetBucketLogging response. A bucket that logs to itself is not counted.

logging_required_bucket_count.description: Buckets that are not a server access log destination, the population logging_enabled covers.
logging_required_bucket_count.x-epack-summary: Number of buckets that do not receive other buckets' access logs. Access logging is measured over these buckets.

account_public_access_block_enabled.description: Whether the account-level S3 Block Public Access settings set all four flags.
account_public_access_block_enabled.x-epack-summary: Whether all four Block Public Access flags are on at the account level. When they are, every bucket in the account blocks public access whatever its own settings.
account_public_access_block_enabled.x-epack-method: Calls the S3 Control GetPublicAccessBlock for the account and checks that all four flags are on.

buckets.description: Audit level and above: one row per bucket, up to 10,000. Past the cap, the first by name are kept.
buckets.x-epack-summary: Per-bucket rows the storage percentages were computed from. Capped at 10,000 buckets.

RDSMetrics.description: RDS databases across the scanned regions. The figures cover the regions whose listing succeeded, and are meaningful only when regions_failed is absent.

regions_evaluated_count.description: Regions whose RDS listing succeeded. The aggregates cover only these regions and are meaningful only when regions_failed is absent.
regions_evaluated_count.x-epack-summary: How many regions the database scan covered successfully. The percentages cover only these regions.
regions_evaluated_count.x-epack-method: Counts the regions where DescribeDBInstances and DescribeDBClusters both succeeded.

event_subscription_count.description: RDS event subscriptions across the evaluated regions.
event_subscription_count.x-epack-summary: RDS event subscriptions across scanned regions.
event_subscription_count.x-epack-method: Counts the event subscriptions listed by DescribeEventSubscriptions in each region read.

backup_failure_alerting_subscription_cou.description: Enabled subscriptions that would carry a backup failure. Empty event categories cover everything, so subscribe-to-all subscriptions count.
backup_failure_alerting_subscription_cou.x-epack-summary: Enabled event subscriptions that would carry a backup failure. A subscription with no category filter covers everything, so subscribe-to-all setups count here.
backup_failure_alerting_subscription_cou.x-epack-method: Counts the enabled event subscriptions for DB instances or clusters whose event categories are empty or include backup or failure. A subscription whose status is no-permission or topic-not-exist cannot post to its topic and is not counted.

backup_failure_alerting_reaching_subscri.description: Subscriptions where the chain completes: covering backup failures and delivering to a topic with a confirmed subscriber.
backup_failure_alerting_reaching_subscri.x-epack-summary: Subscriptions that cover backup failures and deliver to a topic with at least one confirmed subscriber. Without this, a failed backup can go unnoticed.
backup_failure_alerting_reaching_subscri.x-epack-method: Counts the covering subscriptions whose SNS topic has at least one confirmed subscription in ListSubscriptionsByTopic.

backup_alerting_topics_unresolved_count.description: Covering subscriptions whose topic subscribers could not be read, so their reach is unproven.
backup_alerting_topics_unresolved_count.x-epack-summary: Covering subscriptions whose SNS topic subscribers could not be read. Whether their alerts reach anyone is unproven.
backup_alerting_topics_unresolved_count.x-epack-method: Counts the covering subscriptions whose SNS topic subscriptions could not be listed with ListSubscriptionsByTopic.

event_subscriptions_unresolved_region_co.description: Regions where event subscriptions could not be listed.
event_subscriptions_unresolved_region_co.x-epack-summary: Regions where event subscriptions could not be listed.
event_subscriptions_unresolved_region_co.x-epack-method: Counts the regions where the DescribeEventSubscriptions call failed.

dml_logging_configured_count.description: Postgres instances whose engine configuration logs data changes and exports the log off the instance: pgaudit with write coverage or log_statement at mod or all, parameter group in sync.
dml_logging_configured_count.x-epack-summary: Postgres instances whose engine configuration logs inserts, updates, and deletes, and exports that log off the instance. Per-user overrides inside the database are not visible to any AWS API, so session-level behavior stays a manual check.
dml_logging_configured_count.x-epack-method: Counts the postgres instances whose DescribeDBParameters values load pgaudit with pgaudit.log covering write, or set log_statement to mod or all. The parameter group must also be in sync, and the instance must export its postgresql log to CloudWatch Logs.

dml_logging_not_exported_count.description: Instances logging data changes into a log that never leaves the instance.
dml_logging_not_exported_count.x-epack-summary: Postgres instances that log data changes only to the instance's local log. Without export to CloudWatch Logs, the log is deleted as it rotates.
dml_logging_not_exported_count.x-epack-method: Counts the postgres instances whose in-sync parameters turn on data-change logging through pgaudit or log_statement, without the postgresql log exported to CloudWatch Logs.

dml_logging_pending_count.description: Instances whose logging configuration awaits a reboot: desired, not in force.
dml_logging_pending_count.x-epack-summary: Postgres instances whose parameter group sets data-change logging but has changes waiting for a reboot. They are not counted as configured until the parameter group is in sync.
dml_logging_pending_count.x-epack-method: Counts the postgres instances whose parameters turn on data-change logging through pgaudit or log_statement while the DescribeDBInstances parameter apply status is not in-sync.

dml_logging_not_configured_count.description: Postgres instances whose engine configuration does not log data changes.
dml_logging_not_configured_count.x-epack-summary: Postgres instances whose engine configuration does not log data changes.
dml_logging_not_configured_count.x-epack-method: Counts the postgres instances whose DescribeDBParameters values neither load pgaudit with write coverage nor set log_statement to mod or all.

dml_logging_unknown_count.description: Instances whose parameters could not be read. Unknown is never reported as not configured.
dml_logging_unknown_count.x-epack-summary: Postgres instances whose parameter group could not be read, so their logging state is unknown. They are not counted in any other data-change logging figure.
dml_logging_unknown_count.x-epack-method: Counts the postgres instances whose parameter group could not be read with DescribeDBParameters.

dml_logging_not_classified_count.description: Instances this classifier does not interpret: engines other than postgres, including aurora-postgresql, and members of a Multi-AZ DB cluster, whose settings live in cluster parameter groups.
dml_logging_not_classified_count.x-epack-summary: DB instances on engines other than RDS for PostgreSQL, such as MySQL and aurora-postgresql, and members of a Multi-AZ DB cluster. Their data-change logging is not checked.
dml_logging_not_classified_count.x-epack-method: Counts the DB instances whose DescribeDBInstances engine name does not start with postgres or that name a DBClusterIdentifier.

regions_failed.description: Regions whose RDS listing failed. Absent when every region evaluated.
regions_failed.x-epack-summary: Regions the database scan could not read. When any region is listed here the account's database figures are incomplete.

database_count.description: Clusters plus the instances outside a DB cluster across evaluated regions, so vacuous aggregates (zero databases) are distinguishable from real ones.
database_count.x-epack-summary: DB clusters plus the DB instances that are not part of a DB cluster, across the regions read. A cluster and its instances count as one database. This covers Aurora, Multi-AZ DB clusters, DocumentDB and Neptune. The database percentages are shares of this number, so with no databases they are absent.
database_count.x-epack-method: Adds the clusters listed by DescribeDBClusters to the DB instances listed by DescribeDBInstances. An instance whose DBClusterIdentifier names a listed cluster is left out.

instance_count.description: DB instances across the evaluated regions, cluster instances included.
instance_count.x-epack-summary: DB instances across the regions read, without the clusters. The publicly reachable percentage is a share of this number.
instance_count.x-epack-method: Counts the DB instances listed by DescribeDBInstances.

encrypted_at_rest.description: Percentage of databases with storage encrypted at rest. Null when there are none.
encrypted_at_rest.x-epack-summary: Share of databases encrypted at rest. Encryption at rest is set at creation and cannot be added later, so a low figure is hard to remediate.
encrypted_at_rest.x-epack-method: Divides encrypted_at_rest_database_count by database_count and rounds down.

encrypted_at_rest_database_count.description: Databases with storage encrypted at rest.
encrypted_at_rest_database_count.x-epack-summary: Number of databases with storage encrypted at rest. Divided by the database count and rounded down, it gives the Databases encrypted percentage.
encrypted_at_rest_database_count.x-epack-method: Counts the DB instances and clusters in DescribeDBInstances and DescribeDBClusters whose StorageEncrypted is true or whose StorageEncryptionType is sse-rds. Storage encrypted with an AWS owned key has StorageEncrypted false and StorageEncryptionType sse-rds. A DB cluster's instances are left out, since the cluster sets this for them.

publicly_accessible.description: Percentage of DB instances that are publicly accessible. Null when there are none.
publicly_accessible.x-epack-summary: Share of DB instances marked publicly accessible, which gives each one a public address. Whether the internet can connect depends on their security groups.
publicly_accessible.x-epack-method: Divides publicly_accessible_instance_count by instance_count and rounds down.

publicly_accessible_instance_count.description: DB instances that are publicly accessible.
publicly_accessible_instance_count.x-epack-summary: Number of DB instances marked publicly accessible. Divided by the database instances and rounded down, it gives the Databases publicly accessible percentage.
publicly_accessible_instance_count.x-epack-method: Counts the DB instances whose PubliclyAccessible is true in DescribeDBInstances.

deletion_protection.description: Percentage of databases with deletion protection on. Null when there are none.
deletion_protection.x-epack-summary: Share of databases guarded against accidental deletion.
deletion_protection.x-epack-method: Divides deletion_protection_database_count by database_count and rounds down.

deletion_protection_database_count.x-epack-summary: Number of databases with deletion protection on. Divided by the database count and rounded down, it gives the Databases delete-protected percentage.
deletion_protection_database_count.x-epack-method: Counts the DB instances and clusters whose DeletionProtection is true in DescribeDBInstances and DescribeDBClusters. A DB cluster's instances are left out, since the cluster sets this for them.

backup_retention_adequate.description: Percentage of databases keeping automated backups for at least 7 days. Null when there are none.
backup_retention_adequate.x-epack-summary: Share of databases keeping automated backups for at least seven days.
backup_retention_adequate.x-epack-method: Divides backup_retention_adequate_database_count by database_count and rounds down.

backup_retention_adequate_database_count.description: Databases keeping automated backups for at least 7 days.
backup_retention_adequate_database_count.x-epack-summary: Number of databases keeping automated backups for at least seven days. Divided by the database count and rounded down, it gives the Backups kept 7+ days percentage.
backup_retention_adequate_database_count.x-epack-method: Counts the DB instances and clusters whose BackupRetentionPeriod is 7 days or more. A DB cluster's instances are left out, since the cluster sets this for them.

backup_retention_min.description: The shortest automated backup retention across the databases, in days. Null when there are no databases.
backup_retention_min.x-epack-summary: The shortest automated backup retention across the databases, in days. A value of 0 means at least one database has automated backups turned off.
backup_retention_min.x-epack-method: Takes the lowest BackupRetentionPeriod across the DB instances and clusters from DescribeDBInstances and DescribeDBClusters. A DB cluster's instances are left out, since the cluster sets this for them.

multi_az_enabled.description: Percentage of databases with a standby or replicas in another availability zone. Null when there are none.
multi_az_enabled.x-epack-summary: Share of databases replicated across more than one availability zone for failover.
multi_az_enabled.x-epack-method: Divides multi_az_enabled_database_count by database_count and rounds down.

multi_az_enabled_database_count.description: Databases with a standby or replicas in another availability zone.
multi_az_enabled_database_count.x-epack-summary: Number of databases with a standby or replicas in another availability zone. Divided by the database count and rounded down, it gives the Databases multi-AZ percentage.
multi_az_enabled_database_count.x-epack-method: Counts the DB instances and clusters whose MultiAZ is true in DescribeDBInstances and DescribeDBClusters. A DB cluster's instances are left out, since the cluster sets this for them.

db_port_open_to_internet_count.description: Instances whose security groups allow ingress from the internet on the database's listening port. Unevaluated instances are excluded; reachability there is unproven, not open.
db_port_open_to_internet_count.x-epack-label: Databases open to the internet on their port
db_port_open_to_internet_count.x-epack-summary: DB instances whose security groups allow any address, 0.0.0.0/0 or ::/0, on the database's listening port. Instances whose ingress could not be checked are left out of this count.
db_port_open_to_internet_count.x-epack-method: Counts the DB instances with a DescribeSecurityGroups ingress rule from 0.0.0.0/0 or ::/0 that covers the instance's endpoint port. A rule that allows a managed prefix list counts when GetManagedPrefixListEntries returns 0.0.0.0/0 or ::/0 for that list.

db_port_ingress_unevaluated_count.description: Instances whose database-port ingress could not be evaluated: no endpoint port yet, or the security groups could not be read.
db_port_ingress_unevaluated_count.x-epack-summary: DB instances whose database-port ingress could not be checked. Either the instance has no endpoint port or security groups yet, or its security groups could not be read.
db_port_ingress_unevaluated_count.x-epack-method: Counts the DB instances that have no endpoint port or security groups, or whose security groups could not be read with DescribeSecurityGroups.

instances.description: Audit level and above: one row per DB instance.
instances.x-epack-summary: Per-instance rows the database percentages were computed from.

clusters.description: Audit level and above: one row per DB cluster.
clusters.x-epack-summary: Per-cluster rows for Aurora and other clustered engines. Public access is set on each member instance, so cluster rows have no public-access field.

NetworkMetrics.description: VPCs and security groups across the scanned regions. The figures cover the regions whose listing succeeded, and are meaningful only when regions_failed is absent: partial coverage can only understate exposure.

regions_evaluated_count.description: Regions whose network listing succeeded. The exposure aggregates cover only these regions and are meaningful only when regions_failed is absent: partial coverage can only understate exposure.
regions_evaluated_count.x-epack-summary: How many regions the network scan covered successfully.
regions_evaluated_count.x-epack-method: Counts the regions where DescribeVpcs and DescribeSecurityGroups both succeeded.

regions_failed.description: Regions whose network listing failed. Absent when every region evaluated.
regions_failed.x-epack-summary: Regions the network scan could not read. A failed region could hold exposed rules, so any entry here means the exposure figures are incomplete.

security_group_count.description: Security groups across the evaluated regions.
security_group_count.x-epack-summary: Security groups across the regions read. The SSH and RDP percentages are shares of this number, so with none they are absent.
security_group_count.x-epack-method: Counts the security groups listed by DescribeSecurityGroups in each region read.

open_to_world_ssh.description: Percentage of security groups allowing SSH (TCP 22) from anywhere, 0.0.0.0/0 or ::/0, including all-traffic rules. Null when there are no security groups.
open_to_world_ssh.x-epack-summary: Share of security groups that allow SSH (port 22) from any address, counting rules that allow all traffic. Higher is worse, since open SSH is a common entry point for attackers.
open_to_world_ssh.x-epack-method: Divides open_to_world_ssh_security_group_count by security_group_count and rounds down.

open_to_world_ssh_security_group_count.description: Security groups allowing SSH (TCP 22) from anywhere, 0.0.0.0/0 or ::/0, including all-traffic rules.
open_to_world_ssh_security_group_count.x-epack-summary: Number of security groups that allow SSH (port 22) from any address, including rules that allow all traffic. Divided by the security groups and rounded down, it gives the SSH open to internet percentage.
open_to_world_ssh_security_group_count.x-epack-method: Counts the security groups with a DescribeSecurityGroups ingress rule from 0.0.0.0/0 or ::/0 that covers TCP port 22, including all-traffic rules. A rule from a managed prefix list counts when the list's entries from GetManagedPrefixListEntries include 0.0.0.0/0 or ::/0.

open_to_world_rdp.description: Percentage of security groups allowing RDP (TCP 3389) from anywhere, 0.0.0.0/0 or ::/0, including all-traffic rules. Null when there are no security groups.
open_to_world_rdp.x-epack-summary: Share of security groups that allow Windows remote desktop (port 3389) from any address, counting rules that allow all traffic. Higher is worse.
open_to_world_rdp.x-epack-method: Divides open_to_world_rdp_security_group_count by security_group_count and rounds down.

open_to_world_rdp_security_group_count.description: Security groups allowing RDP (TCP 3389) from anywhere, 0.0.0.0/0 or ::/0, including all-traffic rules.
open_to_world_rdp_security_group_count.x-epack-summary: Number of security groups that allow remote desktop (port 3389) from any address, including rules that allow all traffic. Divided by the security groups and rounded down, it gives the RDP open to internet percentage.
open_to_world_rdp_security_group_count.x-epack-method: Counts the security groups with a DescribeSecurityGroups ingress rule from 0.0.0.0/0 or ::/0 that covers TCP port 3389, including all-traffic rules. A rule from a managed prefix list counts when the list's entries from GetManagedPrefixListEntries include 0.0.0.0/0 or ::/0.

vpcs.description: Audit level and above: one row per VPC.
vpcs.x-epack-summary: Per-VPC inventory rows. Flow log status is included only at internal level.

security_groups.description: Audit level and above: one row per security group.
security_groups.x-epack-summary: Per-security-group rows, with whether each group allows SSH or RDP from any address.

cloudtrail.description: CloudTrail trails, their logging status, and their delivery buckets.
cloudtrail.x-epack-summary: CloudTrail trails that record API activity in the account, with their logging status and delivery buckets.

trail_buckets_retained_indefinitely_coun.description: Trail delivery buckets with no covering lifecycle expiration: audit logs are kept until someone deletes them. Meets a retain-for-N requirement and fails a delete-after-N one.
trail_buckets_retained_indefinitely_coun.x-epack-summary: Trail delivery buckets with no covering lifecycle expiration, so audit logs are kept until someone deletes them. That meets a requirement to retain logs for a period, and fails one to delete them after a period.
trail_buckets_retained_indefinitely_coun.x-epack-method: Counts the trail buckets whose GetBucketLifecycleConfiguration rules include no enabled expiration covering the AWSLogs/ path of any trail that delivers there.

trail_buckets_expiring_count.description: Trail delivery buckets whose lifecycle rules expire the trail's objects after a number of days.
trail_buckets_expiring_count.x-epack-summary: Trail delivery buckets where a lifecycle rule deletes a delivering trail's objects after a number of days. A bucket that several trails share counts here when any of their objects expire.
trail_buckets_expiring_count.x-epack-method: Counts the trail buckets with an enabled GetBucketLifecycleConfiguration rule that expires objects after a number of days and whose prefix is empty or a prefix of a delivering trail's AWSLogs/ path. For an organization trail, a rule on an AWSLogs/<organization ID>/ folder also counts. A rule that also filters by tag or object size does not count. In a versioned bucket, a covering rule must also expire noncurrent versions without keeping any newer ones.

trail_bucket_min_expiration_days.description: The shortest covering expiration across trail buckets: the binding retention number. Transitions to colder storage preserve data and are not counted as expiration.
trail_bucket_min_expiration_days.x-epack-summary: The shortest covering expiration across trail buckets, which is the number to compare against a retention requirement. Transitions to colder storage preserve the data, so they are not counted as deletion.
trail_bucket_min_expiration_days.x-epack-method: Takes the smallest expiration in days among the enabled lifecycle rules that cover a trail's AWSLogs/ path in the expiring buckets. A bucket's default object lock retention raises its expiration to the retention period, since a lifecycle rule cannot delete a locked object version.

trail_buckets_not_in_account_count.description: Delivery buckets outside this account, the normal shape for organization trails delivering to a log archive account. Enroll that account to make them readable.
trail_buckets_not_in_account_count.x-epack-summary: Delivery buckets missing from this account's bucket list, which is typical for organization trails that deliver to a log archive account. Enrolling that account in collection makes their retention readable.
trail_buckets_not_in_account_count.x-epack-method: Counts the trail buckets missing from this account's ListBuckets results.

trail_buckets_retention_unknown_count.description: Delivery buckets whose lifecycle could not be read, or that expire the trail's objects only on a set date rather than after a number of days.
trail_buckets_retention_unknown_count.x-epack-summary: Delivery buckets whose region or lifecycle could not be read, or whose trail objects expire only on a fixed date. Their retention is unknown.
trail_buckets_retention_unknown_count.x-epack-method: Counts the trail buckets where GetBucketLocation or GetBucketLifecycleConfiguration failed, or where the covering rules expire trail objects only on a date.

trail_buckets_object_locked_count.description: Delivery buckets with object lock default retention: nobody shortens audit log retention, not even an administrator when the mode is COMPLIANCE.
trail_buckets_object_locked_count.x-epack-summary: Delivery buckets with a default object lock retention. In compliance mode nobody can shorten audit log retention, including administrators.
trail_buckets_object_locked_count.x-epack-method: Counts the trail buckets where GetObjectLockConfiguration returns a default retention rule.

trail_buckets_public_access_blocked_coun.description: Delivery buckets with an effective public access block: each of its flags set at the account level or the bucket level.
trail_buckets_public_access_blocked_coun.x-epack-summary: Delivery buckets with an effective public access block, whether from the account level or the bucket itself.
trail_buckets_public_access_blocked_coun.x-epack-method: Counts the trail buckets where each of the four public access block flags is set on the account by S3 Control GetPublicAccessBlock or on the bucket by S3 GetPublicAccessBlock.

trail_buckets_public_access_not_blocked_.description: Delivery buckets with no effective public access block. A trail bucket has no legitimate public readership, so this is an unambiguous finding. The block is the shield: bucket policy and ACL exposure are examined separately at internal level.
trail_buckets_public_access_not_blocked_.x-epack-label: Trail buckets not blocking public access
trail_buckets_public_access_not_blocked_.x-epack-summary: Delivery buckets with no effective public access block. CloudTrail writes through its own service principal, so a trail bucket never needs public access.
trail_buckets_public_access_not_blocked_.x-epack-method: Counts the trail buckets where both public access blocks were read and at least one of the four flags is set on neither.

trail_buckets_public_access_unknown_coun.description: Delivery buckets whose block state could not be fully read. Not-blocked needs both the account and bucket sides known, because the unreadable side could set the flags the other lacks.
trail_buckets_public_access_unknown_coun.x-epack-label: Trail buckets with unknown public access
trail_buckets_public_access_unknown_coun.x-epack-summary: Delivery buckets whose block state could not be fully read. Declaring a bucket open needs both the account and bucket sides known, because the unreadable side could be the one that blocks.
trail_buckets_public_access_unknown_coun.x-epack-method: Counts the trail buckets not fully blocked by the settings that were read, where GetBucketLocation or the account or bucket GetPublicAccessBlock call failed.

trail_listing_evaluated.description: True when the trail listing was collected. The summary booleans are meaningful only when true; on listing failure they are null.
trail_listing_evaluated.x-epack-summary: Whether the trail listing was read in at least one scanned region. When it could not be read anywhere, the logging values are left out.
trail_listing_evaluated.x-epack-method: Records whether DescribeTrails succeeded in any scanned region.

trail_listing_error_code.description: Present when the trail listing was not evaluated.
trail_listing_error_code.x-epack-summary: Why the trail listing could not be read, when applicable.

enabled.description: Whether any trail is logging the management events that change the account.
enabled.x-epack-summary: Whether any CloudTrail trail is logging management events that change the account. A trail that logs only data events or only read events does not count. A trail that leaves out KMS or RDS Data API events does not count either. In a member account that is denied its organization trail's status or event selectors, that trail counts and is marked inferred.
enabled.x-epack-method: Calls DescribeTrails in each scanned region, then GetTrailStatus and, for a trail with custom event selectors, GetEventSelectors. Is true when a logging trail's selectors record write management events from every event source, counting an organization trail whose status or selectors a member account is denied.

multi_region_enabled.description: Whether a multi-region trail is logging the management events that change the account.
multi_region_enabled.x-epack-summary: Whether at least one logging trail records management events that change the account in every region. A multi-region trail that is stopped, or that logs only data events or only read events, does not count. A multi-region trail with global service events off does not count either, since it records no IAM changes.
multi_region_enabled.x-epack-method: Is true when a trail that counts for enabled has IsMultiRegionTrail set in DescribeTrails and IncludeGlobalServiceEvents not set to false.

organization_trail_enabled.description: Whether an organization trail is logging.
organization_trail_enabled.x-epack-summary: Whether an organization-wide trail is logging the management events that change this account. Org trails are set centrally by the management account and cover member accounts uniformly.
organization_trail_enabled.x-epack-method: Is true when a trail that counts for enabled has IsOrganizationTrail set in DescribeTrails.

trail_status_evaluated_count.description: Trails whose logging status was read.
trail_status_evaluated_count.x-epack-summary: How many trails had their logging status read directly.
trail_status_evaluated_count.x-epack-method: Counts the trails from DescribeTrails, once per ARN, whose GetTrailStatus call returned IsLogging.

trail_status_inferred_count.description: Trail statuses inferred from organization shadow-trail presence when the member account could not read GetTrailStatus.
trail_status_inferred_count.x-epack-summary: How many trails were assumed to be logging from organization-trail presence because this account could not read their status directly. Inferred logging is weaker evidence than a confirmed read.
trail_status_inferred_count.x-epack-method: Counts the organization trails whose GetTrailStatus call was denied or failed with TrailNotFoundException, which the collector treats as logging.

trail_status_unknown_count.description: Trails whose logging status could not be read or inferred.
trail_status_unknown_count.x-epack-summary: How many trails had a status that could not be read or inferred.
trail_status_unknown_count.x-epack-method: Counts the trails whose GetTrailStatus call failed and whose logging could not be inferred.

trails.description: Audit level and above: one row per trail, an organization trail once.
trails.x-epack-summary: Per-trail rows the logging booleans were derived from.

config.description: AWS Config in the primary region. That is the first configured region, or else the region the collector signs in to when it is enabled.
config.x-epack-summary: AWS Config recording of resource configuration changes in the primary region.

enabled.x-epack-summary: Whether AWS Config has a configuration recorder in the primary region.
enabled.x-epack-method: Calls DescribeConfigurationRecorders in the primary region and is true when it returns any recorder.

recorder_running.description: Whether a configuration recorder is recording.
recorder_running.x-epack-summary: Whether a configuration recorder in the primary region is recording. Recorders in other regions are not read.
recorder_running.x-epack-method: Calls DescribeConfigurationRecorderStatus in the primary region and is true when any recorder's Recording is true.

recorders.description: Audit level and above: one row per configuration recorder.
recorders.x-epack-summary: One row per configuration recorder in the primary region.

rules.description: Internal level only: one row per rule with its compliance, up to 1,000. Past the cap, the first by name are kept.
rules.x-epack-summary: One row per Config rule in the primary region with its compliance state, up to 1,000. Past the cap, the first rules by name are kept. Rules are listed whether or not the region has a recorder.

rules_truncated.description: Whether the rule list was cut at 1,000 rules.
rules_truncated.x-epack-summary: Whether the rule list was cut off at the cap. If true, the inventory is partial.
rules_truncated.x-epack-method: Is true when DescribeConfigRules returns more than 1,000 rules in the primary region. It is left out when the rules could not be read.

rules_dropped_count.description: Rules left out past the cap.
rules_dropped_count.x-epack-summary: How many rules were omitted past the cap.
rules_dropped_count.x-epack-method: Subtracts 1,000 from the number of rules DescribeConfigRules returns in the primary region, when that number is over 1,000. It is left out when the rules could not be read.

guardduty.x-epack-summary: GuardDuty threat detection across the scanned regions, covering signs of compromise in logs and network activity.

enabled.description: Whether a GuardDuty detector exists in any scanned region.
enabled.x-epack-summary: Whether a GuardDuty detector exists in at least one scanned region. A suspended detector counts too, and its status is on its detector row.
enabled.x-epack-method: Calls ListDetectors in each scanned region and is true when any region returns a detector, whatever its status.

enabled_in_all_regions.description: Whether every scanned region has a GuardDuty detector whose status is ENABLED.
enabled_in_all_regions.x-epack-summary: Whether GuardDuty is on in every scanned region. A region with no detector or a suspended one makes this false.
enabled_in_all_regions.x-epack-method: Calls ListDetectors and GetDetector in each scanned region and is true when every region has a detector whose status is ENABLED.

unremediated_findings_over_48h.description: Unarchived findings of severity 7 or higher, high or critical, last updated more than 48 hours ago, across the detectors.
unremediated_findings_over_48h.x-epack-summary: Unarchived high or critical GuardDuty findings last updated more than 48 hours ago, summed across detectors. A finding that recurs gets a new update time and leaves this count.
unremediated_findings_over_48h.x-epack-method: Sums, across detectors, the ListFindings count of unarchived findings with severity 7 or higher and an updatedAt more than 48 hours before collection. Only the account's own findings count. Sample findings count until they are archived.

finding_notification.description: Whether findings are routed anywhere a person would see them. GuardDuty publishes findings to the regional default EventBridge bus; these fields summarise the rules pointed at it, region by region. Routed means an enabled matching rule with at least one target; reaching a subscriber additionally requires an SNS target with a confirmed subscription. Rules notifying through Lambda or an API destination count as routed but never as reaching, since delivery beyond the invocation is not observable from configuration. In organizations, member accounts commonly route findings centrally: administrator_account_id present explains detector regions with no local rules.
finding_notification.x-epack-summary: Whether GuardDuty findings in each detector region reach a person, read from the EventBridge rules on that region's default bus. Findings reach someone only through an SNS topic with a confirmed subscription.

rule_count.description: Enabled or disabled rules matching GuardDuty findings, across evaluated detector regions.
rule_count.x-epack-summary: EventBridge rules, enabled or not, that match GuardDuty findings in the regions checked.
rule_count.x-epack-method: Counts the default-bus rules from ListRules, in evaluated detector regions, whose event pattern selects GuardDuty findings. The pattern names the source aws.guardduty or the detail-type GuardDuty Finding, and a source or detail-type it lists must include that value.

detector_regions_count.x-epack-summary: Scanned regions with a GuardDuty detector, including a suspended one.
detector_regions_count.x-epack-method: Counts the scanned regions where ListDetectors returns a detector.

detector_regions_evaluated_count.description: Detector regions where the rule listing succeeded. evaluated + unresolved = detector_regions_count.
detector_regions_evaluated_count.x-epack-summary: Detector regions whose rules could be listed. Together with the unchecked regions, this adds up to the regions with a detector.
detector_regions_evaluated_count.x-epack-method: Counts the detector regions where ListRules and ListTargetsByRule succeeded.

detector_regions_unresolved_count.description: Detector regions where the rule listing failed. Excluded from routed/reaching rather than counted as unrouted.
detector_regions_unresolved_count.x-epack-summary: Detector regions whose rules could not be listed. They are left out of the routed and reaching counts.
detector_regions_unresolved_count.x-epack-method: Counts the detector regions where ListRules or ListTargetsByRule failed.

detector_regions_routed_count.description: Detector regions with an enabled rule that matches GuardDuty findings and has a target.
detector_regions_routed_count.x-epack-label: Detector regions with an alert rule
detector_regions_routed_count.x-epack-summary: Detector regions with an enabled rule that matches GuardDuty findings and has a target.
detector_regions_routed_count.x-epack-method: Counts the evaluated detector regions with an enabled matching rule that has at least one target in ListTargetsByRule.

detector_regions_reaching_subscriber_cou.description: Detector regions where such a rule targets an SNS topic with a confirmed subscription.
detector_regions_reaching_subscriber_cou.x-epack-summary: Detector regions with an enabled finding rule that targets an SNS topic with a confirmed subscription. Findings raised in the other detector regions may reach nobody.
detector_regions_reaching_subscriber_cou.x-epack-method: Counts the evaluated detector regions where an enabled matching rule targets an SNS topic with a confirmed subscription in ListSubscriptionsByTopic.

additionalProperties.x-epack-summary: Subscriptions on this channel across the topics that finding rules target.
additionalProperties.x-epack-method: Counts the ListSubscriptionsByTopic entries with this protocol across the SNS topics that matching rules target in evaluated detector regions.

subscriptions_by_protocol.description: Counts only. Subscription endpoints are never collected: they are email addresses, phone numbers, and webhook URLs.
subscriptions_by_protocol.x-epack-summary: Subscriptions on the topics that finding rules target, counted by channel such as email or HTTPS. Subscriber addresses are never collected because they are personal contact details or webhook URLs.

subscriptions_pending_confirmation_count.description: Subscriptions on the targeted topics still waiting for confirmation. They deliver nothing.
subscriptions_pending_confirmation_count.x-epack-summary: Unconfirmed subscriptions on the topics that finding rules target. They deliver nothing until someone confirms them.
subscriptions_pending_confirmation_count.x-epack-method: Counts the ListSubscriptionsByTopic entries whose SubscriptionArn is PendingConfirmation across the SNS topics that matching rules target.

topics_unresolved_count.description: Targeted topics whose subscriptions could not be read.
topics_unresolved_count.x-epack-summary: Topics the rules send to whose subscriptions could not be read, so their reach is unproven.
topics_unresolved_count.x-epack-method: Counts the distinct targeted SNS topics in each region whose ListSubscriptionsByTopic call failed. A deleted topic, for which ListSubscriptionsByTopic returns NotFound, counts as having no subscribers.

administrator_account_id.description: The GuardDuty administrator account when this account is an organization member.
administrator_account_id.x-epack-summary: The account that administers GuardDuty for this one, when it is an organization member. Findings may be routed from there, which explains detector regions with no local rules.

rules.description: Audit level and above: one row per EventBridge rule matching GuardDuty findings.
rules.x-epack-summary: One row per EventBridge rule that matches GuardDuty findings, at audit level and above.

detectors.description: Audit level and above: one row per detector, one per region at most.
detectors.x-epack-summary: One row per GuardDuty detector, at most one per region, with its status and protection settings.

findings.description: Internal level only: unarchived findings of severity 7 or higher, up to 5,000 per detector.
findings.x-epack-summary: Unarchived high or critical findings, one row each, up to 5,000 per detector. When a detector has more, the highest severities are kept. An administrator's member account findings and sample findings are left out.

findings_truncated.description: Whether any detector's findings were cut at 5,000.
findings_truncated.x-epack-summary: Whether the finding list was cut off at the per-detector cap.
findings_truncated.x-epack-method: Is true when ListFindings for any detector has more than 5,000 unarchived findings with severity 7 or higher. It is left out when a detector's findings could not be read and no other detector was cut.

findings_dropped_count.description: Findings left out past the cap.
findings_dropped_count.x-epack-summary: How many findings were omitted past the cap.
findings_dropped_count.x-epack-method: Subtracts the 5,000 findings read from each truncated detector's high_or_critical_findings count and adds the results. It is left out when a truncated detector's count could not be read, or when a detector's findings could not be read.

access_analyzer.description: IAM Access Analyzer coverage, region by region. Only an ACTIVE analyzer analyzes anything, and in an organization the analyzer often lives in a delegated administrator account, so absence here is not absence of coverage.
access_analyzer.x-epack-summary: IAM Access Analyzer coverage for resources shared outside the account, region by region. In an organization the analyzer often lives in a delegated administrator account, so its coverage appears only when that account is enrolled in collection.

enabled.description: Whether an ACTIVE analyzer exists in any scanned region.
enabled.x-epack-summary: Whether at least one analyzer is active in a scanned region. The analyzer's service-linked role can exist without any analyzer running, so the role alone is not evidence.
enabled.x-epack-method: Calls ListAnalyzers in each scanned region and is true when any analyzer's status is ACTIVE.

analyzer_count.description: Analyzers across the evaluated regions, in any status.
analyzer_count.x-epack-summary: Analyzers in any status across the regions whose analyzers were listed.
analyzer_count.x-epack-method: Counts the analyzers from ListAnalyzers across the regions where the listing succeeded.

regions_evaluated_count.x-epack-summary: Regions where the analyzer listing succeeded.
regions_evaluated_count.x-epack-method: Counts the scanned regions where ListAnalyzers succeeded.

regions_with_active_analyzer_count.x-epack-summary: Regions where an active analyzer runs. Coverage is per region, so an analyzer in one region does not cover another.
regions_with_active_analyzer_count.x-epack-method: Counts the scanned regions where ListAnalyzers returns at least one ACTIVE analyzer.

regions_unresolved_count.description: Regions whose analyzers could not be listed.
