regions_unresolved_count.x-epack-summary: Regions where analyzers could not be listed, so coverage there is unproven.
regions_unresolved_count.x-epack-method: Counts the scanned regions where ListAnalyzers failed.

inactive_analyzer_count.description: Analyzers that are creating, disabled, or failed: configuration present, coverage absent.
inactive_analyzer_count.x-epack-summary: Analyzers that are creating, disabled, or failed. They appear in configuration but are not analyzing.
inactive_analyzer_count.x-epack-method: Counts the analyzers from ListAnalyzers whose status is not ACTIVE.

organization_analyzer_present.description: Whether an analyzer of type ORGANIZATION exists.
organization_analyzer_present.x-epack-summary: Whether this account has an organization-wide analyzer in a scanned region, in any status. Organization analyzers live in the management or delegated administrator account.
organization_analyzer_present.x-epack-method: Is true when ListAnalyzers returns an analyzer of type ORGANIZATION in any scanned region, whatever its status.

active_findings_count.description: Active findings across the ACTIVE analyzers.
active_findings_count.x-epack-summary: Active findings across the active analyzers whose findings could be listed. A finding stays active until it is archived or the access is removed.
active_findings_count.x-epack-method: Sums the ListFindings and ListFindingsV2 results with status ACTIVE over the ACTIVE analyzers whose findings could be listed. An IAM role finding appears in every region with an analyzer, so it counts once for each analyzer type. An unused access finding does not change by region, so it also counts once for each analyzer type.

archived_findings_count.description: Archived findings mean someone triages them; a pile of stale active findings means nobody looks.
archived_findings_count.x-epack-summary: Archived findings across the active analyzers whose findings could be listed. A finding is archived by hand or by an archive rule, usually because the access is intended.
archived_findings_count.x-epack-method: Sums the ListFindings and ListFindingsV2 results with status ARCHIVED over the ACTIVE analyzers whose findings could be listed. An IAM role finding appears in every region with an analyzer, so it counts once for each analyzer type. An unused access finding does not change by region, so it also counts once for each analyzer type.

analyzers_with_unresolved_findings_count.description: Active analyzers whose findings could not be listed. Excluded from the finding counts rather than counted as zero.
analyzers_with_unresolved_findings_count.x-epack-summary: Active analyzers whose findings could not be listed. Their findings are left out of the active and archived counts.
analyzers_with_unresolved_findings_count.x-epack-method: Counts the ACTIVE analyzers whose ListFindings call failed.

analyzers.description: Audit level and above: one row per analyzer.
analyzers.x-epack-summary: Per-analyzer rows at audit level and above.

security_hub.description: Security Hub in the primary region, and the CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark controls it scores. The primary region is the first configured region, or else the region the collector signs in to when it is enabled.
security_hub.x-epack-summary: Security Hub in the primary region, with CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark results from its findings.

enabled.x-epack-summary: Whether Security Hub is enabled in the primary region. When off, no CIS controls are scored.
enabled.x-epack-method: Calls DescribeHub in the primary region and is true when it returns a hub ARN.

auto_enable_controls.description: Whether Security Hub turns on new controls in the subscribed standards automatically. Absent when it does not.
auto_enable_controls.x-epack-summary: Whether new controls in the subscribed standards are turned on automatically. When off, new controls stay disabled until someone enables them.

integration_count.description: Product integrations sending findings to Security Hub.
integration_count.x-epack-summary: Products enabled to send findings to Security Hub in the primary region.

standards_arns.description: Audit level and above: the ARNs of the standards subscribed to.
standards_arns.x-epack-summary: ARNs of the standards this account subscribes to in Security Hub. An empty list with Security Hub enabled means no standard is scored.

product_subscriptions.description: Audit level and above: the ARNs of the product subscriptions that send findings.
product_subscriptions.x-epack-summary: Third-party and AWS products subscribed as finding sources.

cis_aws_foundations_benchmark_level_1.description: CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark level 1 controls, across the subscribed CIS standards.
cis_aws_foundations_benchmark_level_1.x-epack-summary: Compliance against CIS Benchmark Level 1, the baseline profile of broadly applicable, low-friction controls.

cis_aws_foundations_benchmark_level_2.description: CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark level 2 controls, across the subscribed CIS standards.
cis_aws_foundations_benchmark_level_2.x-epack-summary: Compliance against CIS Benchmark Level 2, the stricter profile of defense-in-depth controls for security-sensitive environments.

cis_aws_foundations_benchmark_unknown_le.description: CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark controls whose findings name no profile level.
cis_aws_foundations_benchmark_unknown_le.x-epack-summary: CIS controls whose findings name no profile level. They are scored the same way as the Level 1 and Level 2 controls.

inspector.description: Amazon Inspector, read from its findings in Security Hub in the primary region. EC2 instances are the resources counted.
inspector.x-epack-summary: Amazon Inspector vulnerability findings, read from Security Hub in the primary region. The instance counts cover EC2 only.

status_evaluated.description: True when the Inspector status was read (including a genuine absence). enabled and unpatched_server_percent are meaningful only when true.
status_evaluated.x-epack-summary: Whether the Inspector findings in Security Hub could be read. When they could not, the Inspector values are left out.
status_evaluated.x-epack-method: Records whether Security Hub GetFindings, filtered to Inspector findings in the primary region, succeeded.

status_error_code.description: Present when the Inspector status was not evaluated.
status_error_code.x-epack-summary: Why the Inspector findings in Security Hub could not be read, when applicable.

enabled.description: Whether Security Hub holds any Inspector finding.
enabled.x-epack-summary: Whether Security Hub in the primary region holds any Inspector finding. When Inspector is on but has no findings, this is false.
enabled.x-epack-method: Is true when Security Hub GetFindings in the primary region returns any finding of this account whose product name starts with Inspector.

unpatched_server_percent.description: Percentage of EC2 instances with Inspector findings that have an unpatched finding. Null when no instance has a finding.
unpatched_server_percent.x-epack-summary: Share of EC2 instances with Inspector findings that have at least one finding still open. Instances with no findings are left out of the count.
unpatched_server_percent.x-epack-method: Divides unpatched_resources by total_affected_resources and rounds down.

total_affected_resources.description: EC2 instances with at least one Inspector finding.
total_affected_resources.x-epack-summary: EC2 instances with at least one Inspector finding in Security Hub, open or closed. This is the denominator of the unpatched percentage.
total_affected_resources.x-epack-method: Counts the distinct AwsEc2Instance resources on this account's Inspector findings from Security Hub GetFindings.

unpatched_resources.description: EC2 instances with at least one unpatched finding.
unpatched_resources.x-epack-summary: EC2 instances with at least one open Inspector finding. Divided by affected resources and rounded down, it gives the unpatched percentage.
unpatched_resources.x-epack-method: Counts the distinct AwsEc2Instance resources on this account's Inspector findings that are not archived and whose workflow status is not RESOLVED or SUPPRESSED.

total_findings.x-epack-summary: Inspector findings in Security Hub in the primary region, open or closed, for every resource type.

patched_findings.description: Findings archived, or with a workflow status of RESOLVED or SUPPRESSED.
patched_findings.x-epack-summary: Inspector findings that are archived or marked RESOLVED or SUPPRESSED. A suppressed finding counts here even when the software is still unpatched.

unpatched_findings.description: Findings neither archived nor resolved nor suppressed.
unpatched_findings.x-epack-summary: Inspector findings that are not archived and not marked RESOLVED or SUPPRESSED.

CISComplianceByLevel.description: The CIS controls at one profile level, by their findings' compliance status.

enabled.description: Whether any control at this level has a finding.
enabled.x-epack-summary: Whether any CIS control at this level has a finding in the subscribed CIS standards. Archived and suppressed findings, and a Security Hub administrator's member account findings, do not count. False when Security Hub is off or no CIS standard is subscribed.
enabled.x-epack-method: Is true when the account's own active, unsuppressed GetFindings results for the subscribed CIS standards include a control at this level, by the level named in each finding's RelatedRequirements.

scored_controls.description: Controls passed, failed, or warning, the population compliance_percent covers.
scored_controls.x-epack-summary: CIS controls at this level that passed, failed, or warned. This is the denominator of the compliance percentage.

compliance_percent.description: Percentage of scored controls that passed. Null when none were scored.
compliance_percent.x-epack-summary: Share of scored CIS controls at this level that passed. Null when no control was scored.
compliance_percent.x-epack-method: Divides passed_controls by scored_controls and rounds down.

compliance_state.description: FAILED when any control failed, else WARNING when any warned, else PASSED when any passed, else NOT_AVAILABLE when every control was unavailable, else UNKNOWN.
compliance_state.x-epack-summary: FAILED when any control at this level failed, else WARNING when any warned, else PASSED when any passed. NOT_AVAILABLE means every control was unavailable, and UNKNOWN means none had a finding.

passed_controls.x-epack-summary: CIS controls at this level with a passing finding and no failed or warning finding.
passed_controls.x-epack-method: Counts, per subscribed CIS standard, the controls at this level whose worst compliance status across the account's own active, unsuppressed GetFindings results is PASSED, and adds the standards together.

failed_controls.x-epack-summary: CIS controls at this level with at least one failed finding.
failed_controls.x-epack-method: Counts, per subscribed CIS standard, the controls at this level whose worst compliance status across the account's own active, unsuppressed GetFindings results is FAILED, and adds the standards together.

warning_controls.description: Controls with a warning finding and no failed one.
warning_controls.x-epack-summary: CIS controls at this level with a warning finding and no failed one.
warning_controls.x-epack-method: Counts, per subscribed CIS standard, the controls at this level whose worst compliance status across the account's own active, unsuppressed GetFindings results is WARNING, and adds the standards together.

not_available_controls.description: Controls Security Hub could not check, such as for an unsupported resource.
not_available_controls.x-epack-summary: CIS controls at this level whose findings are all NOT_AVAILABLE. These controls could not be checked, often because the resource they cover is absent.
not_available_controls.x-epack-method: Counts, per subscribed CIS standard, the controls at this level whose worst compliance status across the account's own active, unsuppressed GetFindings results is NOT_AVAILABLE, and adds the standards together.

IdentityCenterStatus.description: AWS IAM Identity Center (formerly AWS SSO) posture.

enabled.description: Whether an Identity Center instance was found in any scanned region. A member account cannot see its organization's instance, so it reads false there.
enabled.x-epack-summary: Whether an Identity Center instance was found in any scanned region. A member account can't see its organization's instance, so it reads false there. It is absent when the config lists the regions and none of them has an instance.
enabled.x-epack-method: Calls SSO Admin ListInstances in each scanned region and sets true when at least one instance comes back. When the config lists the regions and none of them has an instance, it is left out with a not_read gap, since the instance can be in a region not listed.

instance_arn.x-epack-summary: The Identity Center instance identifier. Absent when not enabled.

instance_region.description: The region the instance was found in.
instance_region.x-epack-summary: Region the Identity Center instance is hosted in.

instance_status.description: AWS's status for the instance, such as ACTIVE or CREATE_IN_PROGRESS. Only an active instance signs people in.
instance_status.x-epack-summary: The instance's status, such as Active. Only an active instance can sign people in.

instance_owner_account_id.description: The account that owns the instance: the organization's management account for an organization instance, and this account for an account instance.
instance_owner_account_id.x-epack-summary: The account that owns the instance. For an organization instance it is the organization's management account, and for an account instance it is this account.

instance_type.description: organization for the organization's instance, which signs people in to the organization's AWS accounts, or account for an account instance, which cannot. An instance another account owns is the organization's. Otherwise AWS's answer to the permission set listing decides, since it refuses an account instance.
instance_type.x-epack-summary: Organization when this is the organization's instance, which can sign people in to the organization's AWS accounts. Account when it is an account instance, which can't, so it doesn't count as Identity Center in use.

identity_store_id.description: The ID of the instance's identity store.
identity_store_id.x-epack-summary: Identifier of the backing identity store that holds users and groups.

user_count.x-epack-summary: Number of users in the identity store.
user_count.x-epack-method: Counts the users that Identity Store ListUsers returns for the instance's identity store.

external_id_user_count.description: Identity store users with an external ID from SCIM provisioning, whose issuer is the identity store's provisioning tenant (arn:aws:identitystore::<account>:identitystore/<store id>/provisioningtenant/<tenant id>). IAM Identity Center sets one when an external identity provider provisions a user. An external ID from any other issuer, such as an Active Directory sync, does not count. The IDs and issuers are not collected.
external_id_user_count.x-epack-summary: Number of users with an external ID from SCIM provisioning, which is set when an external identity provider provisions the user. An external ID from any other issuer, such as an Active Directory sync, doesn't count.
external_id_user_count.x-epack-method: Counts the ListUsers users with an external ID whose issuer is an identity store provisioning tenant ARN.

mfa_evidence.description: Where the directory's users' MFA is set. It is external_idp when every user has an external ID from SCIM provisioning, since an external identity provider then signs them in, and manual_required when none does, since Identity Center's own MFA settings then apply. Users synced from Active Directory, or with an external ID from another issuer, count as Identity Center's own. It is unknown for a mix or a directory with no users.
mfa_evidence.x-epack-summary: The value is external_idp when every user was provisioned over SCIM from an external identity provider, and manual_required when none was, so Identity Center's own MFA settings apply. A directory with a mix of the two, or with no users, is unknown.

group_count.x-epack-summary: Number of groups in the identity store.
group_count.x-epack-method: Counts the groups that Identity Store ListGroups returns for the instance's identity store.

permission_set_count.description: Permission sets in the instance. An account instance has none, so the count is left out as not licensed.
permission_set_count.x-epack-summary: Number of permission sets, the templates that define what access a user gets in an account. Absent for an account instance, which has no permission sets.
permission_set_count.x-epack-method: Counts the permission set ARNs that SSO Admin ListPermissionSets returns for the instance.

regions_checked.description: The scanned regions whose Identity Center instance listing answered.
regions_checked.x-epack-summary: Scanned regions where the collector could list Identity Center instances. The organization's instance can be in any region, so the collector checks each one.

permission_sets.description: Audit level and above: one row per permission set.
permission_sets.x-epack-summary: One row per permission set in the instance.

users.description: Audit level and above: one row per identity store user. No personal data beyond the primary email is collected.
users.x-epack-summary: Per-user rows from the identity store.

groups.description: Audit level and above: one row per identity store group, with its direct members.
groups.x-epack-summary: Per-group rows from the identity store.

account_assignments.description: Audit level and above: who holds which permission set in which account, up to 10,000. Past the cap, the first by account, permission set, and principal are kept. Meaningful only when assignments_evaluated is true.
account_assignments.x-epack-summary: One row per grant of a permission set to a user or group in an account, up to 10,000 rows. A reviewer can join them with the user, group and permission set lists to see who can access each account.

assignments_evaluated.description: True when the assignment listing was fully collected. On failure the array is empty and this is false; a partial inventory is never emitted.
assignments_evaluated.x-epack-summary: Whether every account assignment was listed, which happens at audit level and above. When false, no assignment rows are kept.
assignments_evaluated.x-epack-method: Records whether SSO Admin ListAccountAssignments succeeded for every permission set in each account it is provisioned to.

assignments_truncated.description: Whether the assignments were cut at 10,000.
assignments_truncated.x-epack-summary: Whether the assignment list was cut at 10,000 rows. The rows left out are counted in Assignments dropped.
assignments_truncated.x-epack-method: Sets true when ListAccountAssignments returned more than 10,000 assignments in all.

assignments_dropped_count.description: Assignments left out past the cap.
assignments_dropped_count.x-epack-summary: How many assignment rows were dropped by the size cap.
assignments_dropped_count.x-epack-method: Counts the assignments listed beyond the first 10,000.

LambdaMetrics.description: Lambda functions across the scanned regions.

function_count.description: Lambda functions across the scanned regions.
function_count.x-epack-summary: Lambda functions across the scanned regions.
function_count.x-epack-method: Counts the functions listed by ListFunctions in each scanned region.

deprecated_runtime_count.x-epack-summary: Functions on a runtime AWS has deprecated. Deprecated runtimes no longer get security patches.
deprecated_runtime_count.x-epack-method: Counts the functions whose runtime from ListFunctions is on the collector's list of deprecated Lambda runtimes.

public_function_url_count.description: Audit enrichment: functions with a publicly-invokable Function URL (auth_type=NONE).
public_function_url_count.x-epack-summary: Count of functions with a function URL, on the function or on an alias, whose auth type is NONE, meaning anyone on the internet can invoke them.

functions.description: Audit level and above: one row per function, up to 5,000. Past the cap, the most recently modified are kept.

functions_truncated.description: Whether the function list was cut at 5,000.
functions_truncated.x-epack-summary: Whether the function list was cut off at the cap.
functions_truncated.x-epack-method: Set when more than 5,000 functions are listed across all regions at audit level or above.

functions_dropped_count.description: Functions left out past the cap.
functions_dropped_count.x-epack-summary: How many functions were omitted past the cap.
functions_dropped_count.x-epack-method: Subtracts 5,000 from the number of functions listed across all regions at audit level or above, when that number is over 5,000.

EC2Metrics.description: EC2 instances and EBS volumes across the scanned regions.

instance_count.x-epack-summary: Running EC2 instances across the scanned regions. Stopped instances are listed in the inventory but not counted here.
instance_count.x-epack-method: Counts the instances in DescribeInstances whose state is running.

imdsv2_required_count.description: Running instances that require IMDSv2 session tokens.
imdsv2_required_count.x-epack-summary: Running instances that require IMDSv2 session tokens for the metadata service. The rest still allow IMDSv1, which is open to SSRF-style credential theft.
imdsv2_required_count.x-epack-method: Counts the running instances whose DescribeInstances metadata option HttpTokens is required.

public_ip_count.description: Running instances with a public IP address.
public_ip_count.x-epack-summary: Running instances with a public IP address. Whether the internet can reach them depends on their security groups.
public_ip_count.x-epack-method: Counts the running instances with a PublicIpAddress in DescribeInstances.

default_vpc_count.description: Running instances in a default VPC.
default_vpc_count.x-epack-summary: Count of instances running in a default VPC, which ships with permissive networking and is discouraged for production.
default_vpc_count.x-epack-method: Counts the running instances whose VPC is marked IsDefault in DescribeVpcs.

unattached_volume_count.description: EBS volumes attached to no instance. They retain their data and are not covered by the instance figure below.
unattached_volume_count.x-epack-summary: EBS volumes attached to no instance. They keep their data and are not counted in Instances with unencrypted volume.
unattached_volume_count.x-epack-method: Counts the EBS volumes in DescribeVolumes that have no attachments.

unattached_unencrypted_volume_count.description: Unattached volumes without encryption at rest.
unattached_unencrypted_volume_count.x-epack-summary: Unattached volumes without encryption at rest. Nothing is running against these disks, so they tend to be forgotten while still holding data.
unattached_unencrypted_volume_count.x-epack-method: Counts the DescribeVolumes volumes with no attachments whose Encrypted value is false.

instances_with_unencrypted_volume_count.description: Running instances with at least one unencrypted EBS volume attached.
instances_with_unencrypted_volume_count.x-epack-summary: Running instances with at least one unencrypted EBS volume attached. An unencrypted disk exposes its data if a snapshot or copy of it leaks.
instances_with_unencrypted_volume_count.x-epack-method: Counts the running instances with an attached EBS volume whose DescribeVolumes Encrypted value is false.

instances.description: Audit level and above: one row per instance in any state, up to 10,000. Past the cap, the most recently launched are kept.
instances.x-epack-summary: One row per instance, including stopped ones, up to 10,000. Past the cap, the most recently launched are kept.

instances_truncated.description: Whether the instance list was cut at 10,000.
instances_truncated.x-epack-summary: Whether the instance list was cut off at the cap.
instances_truncated.x-epack-method: Sets true when the instance rows from all regions exceed 10,000.

instances_dropped_count.description: Instances left out past the cap.
instances_dropped_count.x-epack-summary: How many instances were omitted past the cap.
instances_dropped_count.x-epack-method: Counts the instance rows past the 10,000 cap, after sorting by launch time with the newest first.

AutoScalingMetrics.description: EC2 auto scaling groups: the instance-based sibling of the ECS capacity evidence.

group_count.description: Auto Scaling groups across the scanned regions.
group_count.x-epack-method: Counts the groups that DescribeAutoScalingGroups returns in each scanned region.

single_instance_group_count.description: Groups whose minimum size is one instance or none: no redundancy at the floor. Sometimes deliberate, as in the bastion pattern where the group exists for self-healing rather than capacity.
single_instance_group_count.x-epack-summary: Groups whose minimum size is one instance or none, so the floor has no redundancy. A bastion group often runs a single instance on purpose so a failed host is replaced.
single_instance_group_count.x-epack-method: Counts the groups whose DescribeAutoScalingGroups MinSize is 1 or less. With instance weights, MinSize is in weight units. When every instance type has the same WeightedCapacity, MinSize is divided by it first and rounded up.

single_zone_group_count.x-epack-summary: Groups confined to one availability zone, so a zone outage takes them down.
single_zone_group_count.x-epack-method: Counts the groups with exactly one availability zone in DescribeAutoScalingGroups.

groups_with_scaling_policy_count.description: Groups with at least one scaling policy. A group without one holds capacity but only changes it when told to.
groups_with_scaling_policy_count.x-epack-summary: Groups with at least one scaling policy. Without one, capacity changes only through manual edits or scheduled actions.
groups_with_scaling_policy_count.x-epack-method: Counts the groups with at least one enabled policy in DescribePolicies. A predictive scaling policy counts only in ForecastAndScale mode, since ForecastOnly makes forecasts and does not scale.

groups_with_suspended_processes_count.description: Groups with scaling processes suspended: the configuration is present but inert.
groups_with_suspended_processes_count.x-epack-summary: Groups with at least one Auto Scaling process suspended. Depending on which process is suspended, the group may stop scaling or stop replacing unhealthy instances.
groups_with_suspended_processes_count.x-epack-method: Counts the groups whose SuspendedProcesses list in DescribeAutoScalingGroups is not empty.

groups_with_elb_health_check_count.description: Groups replacing instances on load balancer health, so an instance is replaced when the application stops answering rather than only when the VM dies.
groups_with_elb_health_check_count.x-epack-label: Groups using load balancer health checks
groups_with_elb_health_check_count.x-epack-summary: Groups whose health check types include ELB, so an instance is also replaced when it fails the load balancer health check. This is the usual setting for a group behind a load balancer.
groups_with_elb_health_check_count.x-epack-method: Counts the groups whose DescribeAutoScalingGroups HealthCheckType, a comma-separated list, includes ELB.

load_balanced_groups_without_elb_health_.description: Load-balanced groups still on EC2-only health checks. The target group stops routing to a hung application, but the instance is never replaced because the VM reports healthy: detection without response.
load_balanced_groups_without_elb_health_.x-epack-label: Load-balanced groups with VM-only health checks
load_balanced_groups_without_elb_health_.x-epack-summary: Load-balanced groups that replace instances only on failed EC2 status checks. An instance with a hung application stops getting traffic but stays in the group until someone replaces it.
load_balanced_groups_without_elb_health_.x-epack-method: Counts the groups with a target group, classic load balancer or traffic source attached whose HealthCheckType list includes neither ELB nor VPC_LATTICE.

groups_on_launch_configurations_count.description: Groups still on launch configurations, which AWS has deprecated in favor of launch templates.
groups_on_launch_configurations_count.x-epack-summary: Groups still using launch configurations, which AWS has deprecated in favor of launch templates.
groups_on_launch_configurations_count.x-epack-method: Counts the groups that DescribeAutoScalingGroups returns with neither a launch template nor a mixed instances policy.

groups.description: Audit level and above: one row per group.
groups.x-epack-summary: Per-group rows at audit level and above.

name.x-epack-summary: Name of the auto scaling group.

min_size.description: The group's MinSize, in instances or, with instance weights, in weight units.
min_size.x-epack-summary: The fewest instances the group will keep, or the fewest weight units when instance types are weighted. The desired capacity changes as scaling acts, but the group never drops below this number.

max_size.description: The most instances the group can scale to.
max_size.x-epack-summary: The most instances the group can scale out to.

desired_capacity.description: The instances the group is set to run now.
desired_capacity.x-epack-summary: Instances the group is set to run now.

availability_zone_count.description: Availability zones the group launches into.
availability_zone_count.x-epack-summary: How many availability zones the group's instances can run in. With a single zone, a zone outage stops the whole group.

health_check_type.description: What replaces an instance, as a comma-separated list such as EC2 or EBS,ELB. EC2 is the instance's own status, and ELB adds the load balancer's health check.
health_check_type.x-epack-summary: With EC2, an instance is replaced when its EC2 status checks fail. With ELB, it is also replaced when it fails the load balancer health check.

health_check_grace_period_seconds.description: How long a new instance is exempt from health replacement while it boots. Too short causes replacement loops; too long delays detection.
health_check_grace_period_seconds.x-epack-summary: Seconds a new instance is exempt from health replacement while it boots. Too short a period can cause replacement loops, and too long a period delays detection.

uses_launch_template.description: Whether the group launches from a launch template rather than a launch configuration.
uses_launch_template.x-epack-summary: Whether the group launches from a launch template. False means it uses a deprecated launch configuration.

load_balanced.description: Whether the group registers its instances with a load balancer, target group, or traffic source such as a VPC Lattice target group.
load_balanced.x-epack-summary: Whether the group's instances sit behind a target group, classic load balancer, or VPC Lattice target group.

suspended_process_count.description: Scaling processes suspended on the group.
suspended_process_count.x-epack-summary: Scaling processes switched off for this group.

policy_count.x-epack-summary: Policies that move this group's capacity. A disabled policy and a predictive policy in ForecastOnly mode are not counted.

ECSMetrics.description: Container service capacity: how services scale and how deployments fail safe. Task definitions are never read, because container definitions embed environment variables that routinely hold credentials.

cluster_count.description: Clusters running at least one service, across the scanned regions.
cluster_count.x-epack-summary: ECS clusters with at least one service.
cluster_count.x-epack-method: Counts the clusters from ListClusters that have at least one service in ListServices.

service_count.x-epack-method: Counts the services that ListServices returns across every cluster in each scanned region.

fargate_service_count.description: Services on the Fargate launch type.
fargate_service_count.x-epack-summary: Services whose launch type is FARGATE. Services that run on Fargate through a capacity provider strategy have no launch type and are not counted.
fargate_service_count.x-epack-method: Counts the services whose DescribeServices launch type is FARGATE.

services_with_autoscaling_count.description: Services with a registered capacity range.
services_with_autoscaling_count.x-epack-summary: Services with a capacity range registered in Application Auto Scaling. A range alone does not change capacity without a scaling policy.
services_with_autoscaling_count.x-epack-method: Counts the services that have an ECS scalable target in DescribeScalableTargets.

services_with_scaling_policy_count.description: Services where the chain is complete: capacity bounds registered and a policy that moves the service between them.
services_with_scaling_policy_count.x-epack-summary: Services with a registered capacity range and at least one scaling policy that moves the service within it.
services_with_scaling_policy_count.x-epack-method: Counts the services with a scalable target and at least one policy in DescribeScalingPolicies that can change the capacity. A policy does not count when the target's MinCapacity equals its MaxCapacity. A predictive policy counts only in ForecastAndScale mode. A target tracking or step scaling policy does not count while the target's SuspendedState suspends dynamic scaling in and out. A step scaling policy counts only when its Alarms list names an alarm.

single_task_service_count.description: Services whose capacity floor is one task: the scaling minimum where registered, otherwise the desired count. One task is zero redundancy.
single_task_service_count.x-epack-summary: Services whose capacity floor is one task or none, taken from the scaling minimum or else the desired count. When the only task fails, the service is down until a replacement starts.
single_task_service_count.x-epack-method: Counts the services whose DescribeScalableTargets minimum, or DescribeServices desired count when no target is registered, is 1 or less.

services_with_circuit_breaker_count.description: Services whose deployments stop automatically when new tasks fail to become healthy.
services_with_circuit_breaker_count.x-epack-summary: Services whose deployments stop automatically when new tasks fail to become healthy. Without one, ECS keeps retrying a failing deployment until someone stops it.
services_with_circuit_breaker_count.x-epack-method: Counts the services whose DescribeServices deployment circuit breaker is enabled.

services_with_public_ip_count.description: Services whose tasks receive public IP addresses. Zero corroborates a private-subnet architecture.
services_with_public_ip_count.x-epack-summary: Services whose tasks get public IP addresses through awsvpc networking. Tasks on other network modes use the host's address and are never counted.
services_with_public_ip_count.x-epack-method: Counts the services whose DescribeServices awsvpc configuration has AssignPublicIp set to ENABLED.

load_balanced_service_count.description: Services registered with a load balancer.
load_balanced_service_count.x-epack-summary: Services registered with a load balancer or target group.
load_balanced_service_count.x-epack-method: Counts the services with at least one load balancer entry in DescribeServices.

exec_enabled_service_count.description: Services with ECS Exec enabled, which allows an interactive shell into running containers.
exec_enabled_service_count.x-epack-summary: Services with ECS Exec enabled, which allows an interactive shell into running containers.
exec_enabled_service_count.x-epack-method: Counts the services whose DescribeServices EnableExecuteCommand is true.

scaling_unresolved_service_count.description: Services whose scaling state could not be read. Excluded from the capacity findings rather than counted as unscaled.
scaling_unresolved_service_count.x-epack-summary: Services whose scaling state could not be read. They are left out of the scaling and single-task counts.
scaling_unresolved_service_count.x-epack-method: Counts every service in a region where DescribeScalableTargets or DescribeScalingPolicies failed.

services.description: Audit level and above: one row per service.
services.x-epack-summary: Per-service rows at audit level and above.

ECSServiceRow.description: An ECS service. Task definitions are never read.

cluster.description: The cluster the service runs in.

launch_type.description: FARGATE, EC2, or EXTERNAL. Absent when the service uses a capacity provider strategy.
launch_type.x-epack-summary: FARGATE, EC2 or EXTERNAL. Blank when the service uses a capacity provider strategy.

desired_count.description: Tasks the service is set to run.
desired_count.x-epack-summary: Tasks the service is set to keep running.

auto_scaled.description: Whether Application Auto Scaling registers a capacity range for the service.
auto_scaled.x-epack-summary: Whether a capacity range is registered for this service.

min_capacity.description: The fewest tasks auto scaling can scale to, 0 for a service that scales in to none. Absent when not auto scaled.
min_capacity.x-epack-summary: The fewest tasks auto scaling can scale the service in to. Blank when no capacity range is registered.

max_capacity.description: The most tasks auto scaling can scale to. Absent when not auto scaled.
max_capacity.x-epack-summary: The most tasks auto scaling can scale the service out to. Blank when no capacity range is registered.

scaling_policy_types.description: The types of the scaling policies, such as TargetTrackingScaling.
scaling_policy_types.x-epack-summary: The type of each scaling policy on the service, such as TargetTrackingScaling or StepScaling.

scaling_metrics.description: The metrics the scaling policies track, predefined or custom. A custom metric built with metric math is listed by the metrics its queries read.
scaling_metrics.x-epack-summary: Metrics the service's target tracking policies follow, predefined or custom. Metrics behind step scaling policies are not listed.

circuit_breaker_enabled.description: Whether a deployment stops when new tasks fail to become healthy.
circuit_breaker_enabled.x-epack-summary: Whether a failing deployment stops automatically.

circuit_breaker_rollback.description: Whether a stopped deployment rolls back to the last working one.
circuit_breaker_rollback.x-epack-summary: Whether a stopped deployment also rolls back to the last working version.

minimum_healthy_percent.description: The share of desired tasks that must stay healthy during a deployment, in percent. 0 lets every task stop before new ones start. Absent when the service has no deployment configuration.
minimum_healthy_percent.x-epack-summary: Share of desired tasks kept healthy during a deployment.

maximum_percent.description: The most tasks a deployment may run, as a percentage of desired tasks.
maximum_percent.x-epack-summary: Ceiling on tasks during a deployment, as a share of desired.

assigns_public_ip.description: Whether the service's tasks receive public IP addresses.
assigns_public_ip.x-epack-summary: Whether this service's tasks receive public IP addresses.

subnet_count.description: Subnets the service's tasks run in. 0 for a service without awsvpc networking, which names none of its own.
subnet_count.x-epack-summary: Subnets the service's tasks can run in, or 0 for a service without awsvpc networking. Each subnet is in one zone, so the count only approximates zone spread.

load_balanced.description: Whether the service is registered with a load balancer.
load_balanced.x-epack-summary: Whether the service is registered with a load balancer or target group.

execute_command_enabled.description: Whether ECS Exec is on, allowing an interactive shell into running containers.
execute_command_enabled.x-epack-summary: Whether tasks this service launches accept ECS Exec, which opens an interactive shell in the running container.

health_check_grace_period_seconds.description: How long new tasks are exempt from load balancer health replacement while they start.
health_check_grace_period_seconds.x-epack-summary: Seconds new tasks are exempt from load balancer health replacement while they start.

scaling_unresolved.description: Whether the service's scaling could not be read. Absent when it was.
scaling_unresolved.x-epack-summary: Whether this service's scaling state could not be read. One failed read marks every service in the region.

TargetGroupRow.description: A load balancer target group: how the load balancer decides a backend is dead.

region.x-epack-summary: Region the target group lives in.

protocol.description: The protocol to the targets, such as HTTP or TCP.
protocol.x-epack-summary: Protocol the load balancer uses toward these targets.

target_type.description: What the targets are: instance, ip, lambda, or alb.
target_type.x-epack-summary: Instance, IP, Lambda, or ALB targets.

health_check_enabled.x-epack-summary: Whether the load balancer probes these targets for health.

healthy_threshold_count.description: Passing checks in a row before a target counts as healthy.
healthy_threshold_count.x-epack-summary: Consecutive successes before a target counts as healthy.

unhealthy_threshold_count.description: Failing checks in a row before a target counts as unhealthy.
unhealthy_threshold_count.x-epack-summary: Consecutive failures before a target is taken out of rotation.

attached.description: Whether any load balancer uses this target group.
attached.x-epack-summary: Whether any load balancer uses this target group.

SESMetrics.description: Outbound mail transport enforcement. SES attempts TLS on every delivery and falls back to plaintext unless a configuration set says REQUIRE, so only REQUIRE counts as enforced.

configuration_set_count.description: Configuration sets across the scanned regions.
configuration_set_count.x-epack-summary: SES configuration sets across scanned regions.
configuration_set_count.x-epack-method: Counts the configuration sets that ListConfigurationSets returns in each scanned region.

configuration_sets_requiring_tls_count.description: Configuration sets whose TLS policy is REQUIRE, so mail sent through them is never delivered in plaintext.
configuration_sets_requiring_tls_count.x-epack-summary: Configuration sets whose delivery policy is REQUIRE. Mail sent under these is never delivered in plaintext.
configuration_sets_requiring_tls_count.x-epack-method: Counts the configuration sets whose GetConfigurationSet delivery options have a TlsPolicy of REQUIRE.

configuration_sets_opportunistic_tls_cou.description: Sets whose policy is OPTIONAL or unset. Both mean TLS is attempted and plaintext is the fallback.
configuration_sets_opportunistic_tls_cou.x-epack-summary: Configuration sets whose TLS policy is OPTIONAL or unset. SES tries TLS for mail sent through these sets and falls back to plaintext.
configuration_sets_opportunistic_tls_cou.x-epack-method: Counts the configuration sets read with GetConfigurationSet whose TlsPolicy is OPTIONAL or unset.

configuration_sets_unresolved_count.description: Sets whose details could not be read, so their policy is unproven rather than opportunistic.
configuration_sets_unresolved_count.x-epack-summary: Configuration sets whose details could not be read, so their TLS policy is unknown. They are left out of the requiring and opportunistic counts.
configuration_sets_unresolved_count.x-epack-method: Counts the configuration sets whose GetConfigurationSet call failed or came back without a name.

identity_count.description: Sending identities, email addresses and domains, across the scanned regions.
identity_count.x-epack-summary: Email addresses and domains set up as SES identities, including those with sending turned off.
identity_count.x-epack-method: Counts the identities that ListEmailIdentities returns in each scanned region.

identities_requiring_tls_count.description: Sending-enabled identities whose default configuration set requires TLS, so mail naming no set at send time is covered. A send that names its own set can override this; that choice is per message and not visible in config.
identities_requiring_tls_count.x-epack-summary: Sending-enabled identities whose default configuration set requires TLS. A send that names its own configuration set uses that set's policy instead.
identities_requiring_tls_count.x-epack-method: Counts the sending-enabled identities whose GetEmailIdentity default configuration set has a TlsPolicy of REQUIRE.

sending_disabled_identity_count.description: Identities whose sending is turned off.
sending_disabled_identity_count.x-epack-summary: Identities that cannot currently send. Their TLS configuration has no effect until sending is turned back on.
sending_disabled_identity_count.x-epack-method: Counts the identities that ListEmailIdentities returns with SendingEnabled false.

identities_unresolved_count.description: Sending-enabled identities whose details could not be read, so whether they require TLS is unproven.
identities_unresolved_count.x-epack-summary: Sending-enabled identities whose details could not be read, so whether they require TLS is unknown.
identities_unresolved_count.x-epack-method: Counts the sending-enabled identities whose GetEmailIdentity call failed or came back without an identity type.

configuration_sets.description: Audit level and above: one row per configuration set.
configuration_sets.x-epack-summary: Per-set rows at audit level and above.

identities.description: Audit level and above: one row per sending identity.
identities.x-epack-summary: Per-identity rows at audit level and above.

tls_policy.description: REQUIRE or OPTIONAL. Absent when the set declares none, which SES treats as OPTIONAL.
tls_policy.x-epack-summary: REQUIRE enforces TLS delivery. OPTIONAL or blank means plaintext fallback.

unresolved.description: Whether the set's details could not be read. Absent when they were.
unresolved.x-epack-summary: Whether this set's details could not be read.

region.x-epack-summary: Region the identity is set up in.

type.x-epack-summary: Email address, domain or managed domain.

sending_enabled.x-epack-summary: Whether the identity can currently send.

default_configuration_set.description: The configuration set applied to mail that names none.
default_configuration_set.x-epack-summary: The set applied to sends that name none. Blank means SES defaults, which do not require TLS.

default_requires_tls.description: Whether that default set's TLS policy is REQUIRE.
default_requires_tls.x-epack-summary: Whether sends from this identity that name no configuration set must travel over TLS.

unresolved.description: Whether the identity's details could not be read. Absent when they were.
unresolved.x-epack-summary: Whether this identity's details could not be read.

CloudFrontMetrics.description: CloudFront distribution transport enforcement on both hops: viewer to edge, and edge to origin. Meaningful only when distributions_evaluated is true, so an unread account is never mistaken for one with no distributions.

distributions_evaluated.description: Whether the distributions were listed. The other values are meaningful only when true.
distributions_evaluated.x-epack-summary: Whether the distributions could be listed. When false, the distribution counts are left out.
distributions_evaluated.x-epack-method: Records whether ListDistributions returned every page of the account's distributions.

distributions_error_code.description: Why the distributions could not be listed.
distributions_error_code.x-epack-summary: Why the distributions could not be listed, when applicable.

distribution_count.x-epack-summary: Distributions in the account, enabled and disabled. CloudFront is a global service, so there is one count for the whole account.
distribution_count.x-epack-method: Counts the distributions that ListDistributions returns.

disabled_distribution_count.description: Distributions that are switched off. Their configuration is latent, so they are excluded from the findings below.
disabled_distribution_count.x-epack-summary: Distributions that are disabled. A disabled distribution serves no traffic, so it is left out of the transport counts.
disabled_distribution_count.x-epack-method: Counts the distributions whose ListDistributions entry has Enabled set to false.

distributions_allowing_plaintext_viewers.description: Enabled distributions where any cache behavior, default or path-scoped, is set to allow-all. Redirect-to-HTTPS and HTTPS-only both deliver content over TLS.
distributions_allowing_plaintext_viewers.x-epack-summary: Enabled distributions where the default or any path-specific cache behavior serves HTTP without redirecting to HTTPS.
distributions_allowing_plaintext_viewers.x-epack-method: Counts the enabled distributions with any cache behavior whose ViewerProtocolPolicy is allow-all.

distributions_with_http_only_origin_coun.description: Enabled distributions fetching from at least one custom origin over plaintext regardless of the viewer policy.
distributions_with_http_only_origin_coun.x-epack-summary: Enabled distributions with at least one origin fetched over HTTP regardless of how the viewer connected. An encrypted browser connection does not make this hop encrypted.
distributions_with_http_only_origin_coun.x-epack-method: Counts the enabled distributions with at least one custom origin or VPC origin whose OriginProtocolPolicy is http-only. A VPC origin's policy is read with GetVpcOrigin. It is left out when a VPC origin could not be read and no other origin of the distribution settles it.

distributions_with_match_viewer_origin_c.description: Enabled distributions whose origin fetch mirrors the viewer's scheme, so the origin hop is plaintext whenever the viewer request was.
distributions_with_match_viewer_origin_c.x-epack-summary: Enabled distributions with at least one custom origin or VPC origin set to match the viewer's protocol. That origin is fetched over HTTP whenever the viewer used HTTP.
distributions_with_match_viewer_origin_c.x-epack-method: Counts the enabled distributions with at least one custom origin or VPC origin whose OriginProtocolPolicy is match-viewer. A VPC origin's policy is read with GetVpcOrigin. It is left out when a VPC origin could not be read and no other origin of the distribution settles it.

additionalProperties.x-epack-summary: Enabled distributions whose minimum viewer TLS policy is this version.
additionalProperties.x-epack-method: Counts the enabled distributions whose ViewerCertificate MinimumProtocolVersion in ListDistributions is this value.

distributions_by_minimum_tls.description: Enabled distributions by minimum viewer TLS version.
distributions_by_minimum_tls.x-epack-summary: Enabled distributions grouped by the oldest TLS version they accept from viewers. Versions before TLSv1.2 are widely considered retired.

distributions.description: Audit level and above: one row per distribution.
distributions.x-epack-summary: Per-distribution rows at audit level and above.

CloudFrontDistributionRow.description: A CloudFront distribution and the protocols on both hops.

aliases.description: The alternate domain names it serves.
aliases.x-epack-summary: Custom domain names the distribution serves.

allows_plaintext_viewers.description: Whether any cache behavior, default or path-scoped, lets viewers use HTTP without a redirect to HTTPS.
allows_plaintext_viewers.x-epack-summary: Whether any of this distribution's behaviors serves HTTP without redirecting.

minimum_protocol_version.description: The oldest TLS version viewers can use, such as TLSv1.2_2021.
minimum_protocol_version.x-epack-summary: Oldest TLS version accepted from viewers.

http_only_origin_count.description: Custom and VPC origins CloudFront fetches from over HTTP only.
http_only_origin_count.x-epack-summary: Origins this distribution always fetches over HTTP.

match_viewer_origin_count.description: Custom and VPC origins fetched over the viewer's protocol, so plaintext whenever the viewer used HTTP.
match_viewer_origin_count.x-epack-summary: Origins fetched with whatever scheme the viewer used.

https_only_origin_count.description: Custom and VPC origins fetched over HTTPS only.

s3_origin_count.description: S3 REST origins, which declare no protocol in config and so are counted rather than classified.
s3_origin_count.x-epack-summary: S3 REST origins on this distribution. They have no origin protocol setting, so they are not in the HTTP or HTTPS origin counts.

LoadBalancerMetrics.description: Load balancer transport enforcement: which hops force TLS toward the client and which accept plaintext.

load_balancer_count.description: Load balancers across the scanned regions.
load_balancer_count.x-epack-summary: Application, network and gateway load balancers across the scanned regions. Classic load balancers are not included.
load_balancer_count.x-epack-method: Counts the load balancers listed by the Elastic Load Balancing v2 DescribeLoadBalancers call in each scanned region.

alb_count.x-epack-summary: Application load balancers, which handle HTTP and HTTPS traffic.
alb_count.x-epack-method: Counts the load balancers whose type from DescribeLoadBalancers is application.

albs_serving_plaintext_count.description: ALBs with at least one HTTP listener whose default action is not a redirect to HTTPS. Listener rules beyond the default action are not inspected.
albs_serving_plaintext_count.x-epack-summary: ALBs with at least one HTTP listener whose default action is something other than a redirect to HTTPS. A redirect that keeps the original scheme counts as plaintext.
albs_serving_plaintext_count.x-epack-method: Counts the ALBs with at least one HTTP listener whose default actions from DescribeListeners include no redirect with protocol HTTPS.

internet_facing_albs_serving_plaintext_c.description: The subset of plaintext-serving ALBs reachable from the internet.
internet_facing_albs_serving_plaintext_c.x-epack-summary: ALBs serving plaintext that have the internet-facing scheme. Anyone on the network path can read HTTP traffic to them.
internet_facing_albs_serving_plaintext_c.x-epack-method: Counts the ALBs in albs_serving_plaintext_count whose scheme is internet-facing.

albs_without_https_listener_count.description: ALBs with readable listeners and no HTTPS listener at all.
albs_without_https_listener_count.x-epack-summary: ALBs whose listeners could be read and include no HTTPS listener, so clients cannot reach them over TLS.
albs_without_https_listener_count.x-epack-method: Counts the ALBs whose DescribeListeners call succeeded and listed no HTTPS listener.

nlb_count.x-epack-summary: Network load balancers, which forward at the connection level.
nlb_count.x-epack-method: Counts the load balancers whose type from DescribeLoadBalancers is network.

nlb_tls_listener_count.description: NLB listeners terminating TLS at the load balancer.
nlb_tls_listener_count.x-epack-summary: NLB listeners that terminate TLS at the load balancer.
nlb_tls_listener_count.x-epack-method: Counts the network load balancer listeners whose protocol from DescribeListeners is TLS.

nlb_tcp_passthrough_listener_count.description: NLB listeners forwarding bytes untouched. Whether the stream is encrypted is decided by the endpoints, not this hop.
nlb_tcp_passthrough_listener_count.x-epack-summary: NLB listeners on TCP, UDP, TCP_UDP, QUIC or TCP_QUIC, which forward traffic without terminating TLS. Whether that traffic is encrypted depends on the client and the backend.
nlb_tcp_passthrough_listener_count.x-epack-method: Counts the network load balancer listeners whose protocol from DescribeListeners is TCP, UDP, TCP_UDP, QUIC or TCP_QUIC.

single_zone_load_balancer_count.description: Load balancers spanning one availability zone: no zone redundancy. ALBs cannot be single-zone by AWS rule, so this in practice counts network load balancers.
single_zone_load_balancer_count.x-epack-summary: Load balancers in only one availability zone, so a zone outage takes them offline. ALBs need at least two zones, so these are network or gateway load balancers.
single_zone_load_balancer_count.x-epack-method: Counts the load balancers with exactly one availability zone in their DescribeLoadBalancers entry.

target_group_count.description: Target groups across the scanned regions.
target_group_count.x-epack-method: Counts the target groups listed by DescribeTargetGroups in each scanned region.

target_groups_without_health_check_count.description: Target groups with health checking off, so the load balancer cannot detect a dead backend.
target_groups_without_health_check_count.x-epack-summary: Target groups with health checks turned off, so traffic still goes to targets that have failed. AWS allows this only for Lambda target groups.
target_groups_without_health_check_count.x-epack-method: Counts the target groups whose HealthCheckEnabled value from DescribeTargetGroups is false. When the answer leaves HealthCheckEnabled out, it is true for target type instance, ip and alb, whose health checks are always on. It is false for lambda, whose default is off.

target_group_listing_failed_region_count.description: Regions where target groups could not be listed, so their health-check posture is unproven.
target_group_listing_failed_region_count.x-epack-summary: Scanned regions where target groups could not be listed. Target groups in those regions are missing from the counts.
target_group_listing_failed_region_count.x-epack-method: Counts the scanned regions where DescribeTargetGroups failed.

additionalProperties.x-epack-summary: Listeners using this security policy, counting both ALB HTTPS and NLB TLS listeners.
additionalProperties.x-epack-method: Counts the listeners from DescribeListeners whose SslPolicy is this policy.

tls_listeners_by_policy.description: TLS-terminating listeners by security policy name. The policy fixes the minimum TLS version the listener accepts.
tls_listeners_by_policy.x-epack-summary: TLS-terminating listeners grouped by security policy, which sets the oldest TLS version accepted. Older policies such as ELBSecurityPolicy-2016-08 still allow TLS 1.0.

listeners_unresolved_count.description: Load balancers whose listeners could not be read, so their transport posture is unproven rather than clean.
listeners_unresolved_count.x-epack-summary: Load balancers whose listeners could not be read, so their transport posture could not be verified.
listeners_unresolved_count.x-epack-method: Counts the load balancers whose DescribeListeners call failed.

load_balancers.description: Audit level and above: one row per load balancer.
load_balancers.x-epack-summary: Per-load-balancer rows at audit level and above.

target_groups.description: Audit level and above: one row per target group.
target_groups.x-epack-summary: Per-target-group rows at audit level and above.

LoadBalancerRow.description: An Elastic Load Balancing load balancer.

name.x-epack-summary: Name given to the load balancer.

region.x-epack-summary: Region the load balancer runs in.

scheme.x-epack-summary: Whether the load balancer faces the internet or only the VPC.

availability_zone_count.description: Availability zones the load balancer serves.
availability_zone_count.x-epack-summary: How many availability zones the load balancer serves from. With a single zone, a zone outage takes it offline.

listeners.description: The load balancer's listeners. Absent when it has none.
listeners.x-epack-summary: The load balancer's listeners and their transport settings.

listeners_unresolved.description: Whether the listeners could not be read. Absent when they were.
listeners_unresolved.x-epack-summary: Whether this load balancer's listeners could not be read. When true, its transport settings are unknown.

port.description: The port the listener accepts connections on. Absent for a Gateway Load Balancer listener, which has none.
port.x-epack-summary: Port the listener accepts connections on.

protocol.description: HTTP, HTTPS, TCP, TLS, UDP, TCP_UDP, QUIC, or TCP_QUIC.
protocol.x-epack-summary: The listener protocol, such as HTTP, HTTPS, TCP, TLS or UDP. An HTTP listener can still move clients to HTTPS with a redirect.

ssl_policy.description: The security policy of a TLS-terminating listener, which fixes the oldest TLS version it accepts.
ssl_policy.x-epack-summary: Security policy on a TLS-terminating listener, which fixes the oldest TLS version accepted.

redirects_to_https.description: Whether the listener's default action redirects to HTTPS.
redirects_to_https.x-epack-summary: Whether the listener's default action redirects to HTTPS. When false on an HTTP listener, the load balancer counts as serving plaintext.

StoredImageMetrics.description: Owned EBS snapshots and AMIs: public exposure and encryption at rest. Volumes attached to running instances are covered under ec2 instead.

snapshot_count.description: Snapshots owned by this account. Snapshots owned by others are never listed.
snapshot_count.x-epack-summary: Owned EBS snapshots across scanned regions.
snapshot_count.x-epack-method: Counts the snapshots from DescribeSnapshots with OwnerIds set to self.

unencrypted_snapshot_count.description: Owned snapshots without encryption at rest.
unencrypted_snapshot_count.x-epack-summary: Snapshots without encryption at rest. A snapshot holds a full copy of a disk, so an unencrypted one carries the same data as the volume it came from.
unencrypted_snapshot_count.x-epack-method: Counts the owned snapshots whose DescribeSnapshots Encrypted value is false.

public_snapshot_count.description: Owned snapshots that anyone can restore.
public_snapshot_count.x-epack-summary: Snapshots any AWS account can restore, which makes their contents effectively public.
public_snapshot_count.x-epack-method: Counts the snapshots from DescribeSnapshots with OwnerIds set to self and RestorableByUserIds set to all.

snapshot_exposure_unknown.description: The public-exposure check failed in at least one region, so a zero public count is unproven rather than clean.
snapshot_exposure_unknown.x-epack-summary: Whether the public snapshot check failed in at least one region. When true, the public snapshot count is left out.
snapshot_exposure_unknown.x-epack-method: Records whether the DescribeSnapshots call with RestorableByUserIds set to all failed in any region.

image_count.x-epack-method: Counts the AMIs from DescribeImages with Owners set to self and IncludeDisabled set, so disabled AMIs count too. An AMI in the deregistered state is not counted.

images_with_unencrypted_volume_count.description: Images with at least one unencrypted EBS device. Instance-store images have no EBS device and are counted in neither direction.
images_with_unencrypted_volume_count.x-epack-summary: Owned AMIs with at least one unencrypted EBS volume. Instances launched from them get unencrypted volumes unless encryption is set at launch or by default.
images_with_unencrypted_volume_count.x-epack-method: Counts the owned AMIs with an EBS block device mapping whose DescribeImages Encrypted value is false.

public_image_count.description: Owned AMIs that anyone can launch.
public_image_count.x-epack-summary: AMIs any AWS account can launch. Anything baked into the image, including credentials left on disk, is readable by anyone.
public_image_count.x-epack-method: Counts the owned AMIs whose DescribeImages Public value is true. An AMI in the deregistered state is not counted.

image_exposure_unknown.description: The AMI lookup failed in at least one region, so a zero public count is unproven.
image_exposure_unknown.x-epack-summary: Whether the AMI listing failed in at least one region. When true, the image counts are left out.
image_exposure_unknown.x-epack-method: Records whether the DescribeImages call with Owners set to self failed in any region.

public_snapshots.description: Audit level and above: one row per owned snapshot anyone can restore.
public_snapshots.x-epack-summary: The snapshots that are publicly restorable, listed so each can be acted on.

public_images.description: Audit level and above: one row per owned AMI anyone can launch.
public_images.x-epack-summary: The AMIs anyone can launch, listed so each can be acted on.

PublicResourceRow.description: A snapshot or AMI anyone can read.

id.x-epack-summary: The ID of the public snapshot or AMI.

name.description: The AMI's name. Absent for a snapshot.
name.x-epack-summary: Name given to the image when it was created.

region.x-epack-summary: Region holding the snapshot or AMI.

encrypted.description: Whether it is encrypted at rest. For an AMI, whether every EBS volume it holds is encrypted. Absent for an AMI with no EBS volume.
encrypted.x-epack-summary: Whether the snapshot is encrypted at rest. For an AMI, true means every EBS volume in the image is encrypted. It is absent for an AMI with no EBS volume, such as an instance-store image.

created_at.description: When the AMI was created. Absent for a snapshot.

MonitoringMetrics.description: CloudWatch alarms and how far their notifications travel. Zero alarms is not evidence that nobody is paged: escalation through EventBridge or a third-party monitor is not visible here.

alarm_count.description: Metric alarms across the scanned regions.
alarm_count.x-epack-summary: CloudWatch metric alarms across scanned regions.
alarm_count.x-epack-method: Counts the metric alarms listed by DescribeAlarms in each scanned region, leaving out composite alarms.

alarms_with_actions_disabled_count.description: Alarms that evaluate but take no action.
alarms_with_actions_disabled_count.x-epack-summary: Alarms with actions turned off. They still change state, but no action runs when they do.
alarms_with_actions_disabled_count.x-epack-method: Counts the alarms whose ActionsEnabled value from DescribeAlarms is false.

alarms_without_notification_count.description: Alarms with no notification topic attached.
alarms_without_notification_count.x-epack-summary: Alarms with no notification topic attached, so firing produces no message.
alarms_without_notification_count.x-epack-method: Counts the alarms with no SNS topic ARN among their AlarmActions from DescribeAlarms.

alarms_insufficient_data_count.description: Alarms that have never had enough data to evaluate.
alarms_insufficient_data_count.x-epack-summary: Alarms currently in the INSUFFICIENT_DATA state, without enough data to evaluate. This often means the metric stopped arriving or the resource is gone.
alarms_insufficient_data_count.x-epack-method: Counts the alarms whose StateValue from DescribeAlarms is INSUFFICIENT_DATA.

alarms_reaching_subscriber_count.description: Alarms whose escalation chain is unbroken: actions enabled, a notification topic attached, and that topic holding at least one confirmed subscriber.
alarms_reaching_subscriber_count.x-epack-summary: Alarms with actions enabled and an SNS topic that has at least one confirmed subscriber. Other alarms can go into ALARM without notifying anyone.
alarms_reaching_subscriber_count.x-epack-method: Counts the alarms with ActionsEnabled true and at least one SNS topic in AlarmActions whose ListSubscriptionsByTopic results include a confirmed subscription.

notification_topic_count.description: Distinct SNS topics the alarms notify whose subscriptions were read.
notification_topic_count.x-epack-summary: Distinct SNS topics in the alarms' actions whose subscriptions could be read.
notification_topic_count.x-epack-method: Counts the distinct SNS topic ARNs in each region's AlarmActions whose ListSubscriptionsByTopic call succeeded.

topics_without_confirmed_subscriber_coun.x-epack-summary: Notification topics with no confirmed subscriber, so alarm messages sent to them reach no one.
topics_without_confirmed_subscriber_coun.x-epack-method: Counts the read topics whose ListSubscriptionsByTopic results hold no confirmed subscription, treating a SubscriptionArn of PendingConfirmation as unconfirmed. A topic for which the call returns NotFound has none.

topics_unresolved_count.description: Topics whose subscriptions could not be read.
topics_unresolved_count.x-epack-summary: SNS topics whose subscriptions could not be read. Alarms are not counted as reaching anyone through these topics.
topics_unresolved_count.x-epack-method: Counts the distinct SNS topics in AlarmActions whose ListSubscriptionsByTopic call failed. A deleted topic, for which ListSubscriptionsByTopic returns NotFound, counts as having no subscribers.

additionalProperties.x-epack-summary: Subscriptions using this protocol on the topics the alarms notify, confirmed or not.
additionalProperties.x-epack-method: Counts the subscriptions with this Protocol in the ListSubscriptionsByTopic results for each topic the alarms notify.

subscriptions_by_protocol.description: Subscriber counts per protocol. Endpoints are never collected: they are personal contact details, and an HTTPS endpoint is routinely a webhook URL that is itself a credential.
subscriptions_by_protocol.x-epack-summary: Subscription counts per protocol, such as email or HTTPS, on the topics the alarms notify. Endpoints are never collected, since they are contact details or webhook URLs that can act as credentials.

subscriptions_pending_confirmation_count.description: Subscriptions that never deliver until confirmed.
subscriptions_pending_confirmation_count.x-epack-summary: Subscriptions on the alarms' topics that are still waiting for confirmation. No messages are delivered to them until someone confirms.
subscriptions_pending_confirmation_count.x-epack-method: Counts the subscriptions whose SubscriptionArn from ListSubscriptionsByTopic is PendingConfirmation.

alarms.description: Audit level and above: one row per alarm.
alarms.x-epack-summary: Per-alarm rows at audit level and above.

alarms_truncated.description: Not emitted: the alarm list is not capped.
alarms_truncated.x-epack-summary: Never emitted, because the collector does not cap the alarm list.
alarms_truncated.x-epack-method: Never set, since the collector keeps every alarm from DescribeAlarms.

alarms_dropped_count.description: Not emitted: the alarm list is not capped.
alarms_dropped_count.x-epack-summary: Never emitted, because the collector does not cap the alarm list.
alarms_dropped_count.x-epack-method: Never set, since the collector keeps every alarm from DescribeAlarms.

namespace.description: The metric's namespace, such as AWS/EC2.
namespace.x-epack-summary: Namespace of the watched metric, such as AWS/EC2 or a custom namespace.

metric_name.description: The metric the alarm watches. For an alarm on an anomaly detection band or a math expression over one metric, that metric.

comparison_operator.description: How the metric is compared with the threshold, such as GreaterThanThreshold.
comparison_operator.x-epack-summary: How the metric is compared against the threshold.

threshold.description: The value the metric is compared with. Absent for an alarm on an anomaly detection band.
threshold.x-epack-summary: The value the metric is compared with. Alarms on an anomaly detection band have none.

evaluation_periods.description: Periods the comparison runs over. Absent for an alarm that uses EvaluationCriteria, such as a PromQL alarm.
evaluation_periods.x-epack-summary: How many of the most recent periods the comparison covers. A PromQL alarm has none.

actions_enabled.description: Whether the alarm's actions run when its state changes.
actions_enabled.x-epack-summary: Whether the alarm's actions run when its state changes.

state_value.x-epack-summary: Whether the alarm is currently OK, alarming, or short of data.

notification_topics.description: Count of SNS topics this alarm notifies.
notification_topics.x-epack-summary: How many topics this alarm publishes to.

reaches_subscriber.description: Whether actions are enabled and a notified topic has a confirmed subscription.
reaches_subscriber.x-epack-summary: Whether the alarm's actions are enabled and one of its SNS topics has a confirmed subscriber.

other_action_count.description: Alarm actions that are not SNS topics, counted but not named.
other_action_count.x-epack-summary: Alarm actions that are not notification topics, such as auto scaling. Counted but not named.

CloudWatchLogsMetrics.description: CloudWatch log groups across the scanned regions. No log content is ever collected.

log_group_count.description: Total log groups across scanned regions.
log_group_count.x-epack-summary: Log groups across the scanned regions.
log_group_count.x-epack-method: Counts the log groups listed by DescribeLogGroups in each scanned region.

log_groups_without_retention_count.description: Log groups with no retention setting, which in CloudWatch Logs means they retain indefinitely. Read as a data-minimisation finding, not a retention gap: a group counted here keeps everything forever, so it satisfies a retain-for-N-months requirement while failing a delete-after-N-months one.
log_groups_without_retention_count.x-epack-summary: Log groups with no retention setting, so their events never expire. That meets a requirement to keep logs for a minimum period and fails one to delete them after a period.
log_groups_without_retention_count.x-epack-method: Counts the log groups from DescribeLogGroups that have no retentionInDays value.

log_groups_without_customer_kms_count.description: Log groups encrypted with an AWS-managed key rather than a customer-managed KMS key.
log_groups_without_customer_kms_count.x-epack-summary: Log groups with no customer managed KMS key, which use the default CloudWatch Logs encryption. With a customer managed key, the account controls who can decrypt the logs.
log_groups_without_customer_kms_count.x-epack-method: Counts the log groups from DescribeLogGroups that have no kmsKeyId.

log_groups.description: Audit level and above: one row per log group, up to 10,000. Past the cap, the largest are kept.
log_groups.x-epack-summary: Per-log-group rows. Capped at 10,000, keeping the largest groups.

log_groups_truncated.description: Whether the log group list was cut at 10,000.
log_groups_truncated.x-epack-summary: Whether the log group list was cut off at the cap.
log_groups_truncated.x-epack-method: Set when more than 10,000 log groups are listed across all regions at audit level or above.

log_groups_dropped_count.description: Log groups left out past the cap.
log_groups_dropped_count.x-epack-summary: How many log groups were omitted past the cap.
log_groups_dropped_count.x-epack-method: Subtracts 10,000 from the number of log groups listed across all regions at audit level or above, when that number is over 10,000.

KMSMetrics.description: KMS posture scoped to CUSTOMER-managed keys only.

customer_managed_key_count.description: Customer managed keys across the scanned regions.
customer_managed_key_count.x-epack-summary: Customer managed KMS keys across the scanned regions.
customer_managed_key_count.x-epack-method: Calls ListKeys and DescribeKey in each scanned region and counts the keys whose KeyManager is CUSTOMER.

cmks_with_rotation_disabled_count.description: Keys KMS can rotate automatically that have automatic rotation off. KMS rotates only symmetric keys whose key material it generated, so asymmetric and HMAC keys, imported key material, and keys in a custom key store are not counted.
cmks_with_rotation_disabled_count.x-epack-summary: Customer managed keys that support automatic rotation and have it turned off. Only symmetric keys with key material generated by KMS can rotate automatically, so other keys are not counted.
cmks_with_rotation_disabled_count.x-epack-method: Calls GetKeyRotationStatus for each customer managed SYMMETRIC_DEFAULT key with AWS_KMS origin and counts those with KeyRotationEnabled false. A key in PendingDeletion or PendingReplicaDeletion is not counted, since KMS reports its rotation as off until the deletion is canceled.

cmks_pending_deletion_count.description: Customer managed keys scheduled for deletion.
cmks_pending_deletion_count.x-epack-summary: Customer managed keys scheduled for deletion. Once a key is deleted, data encrypted under it can no longer be decrypted.
cmks_pending_deletion_count.x-epack-method: Counts the customer managed keys whose DescribeKey KeyState is PendingDeletion, or PendingReplicaDeletion for a multi-Region primary key waiting on its replicas.

keys.description: Audit level and above: one row per customer managed key, up to 5,000. Past the cap, the most recently created are kept.
keys.x-epack-summary: Per-key rows. Capped at 5,000, keeping the most recently created keys.

keys_truncated.description: Whether the key list was cut at 5,000.
keys_truncated.x-epack-summary: Whether the key list was cut off at the cap.
keys_truncated.x-epack-method: Records whether the combined key list across regions had more than 5,000 keys and was cut.

keys_dropped_count.description: Keys left out past the cap.
keys_dropped_count.x-epack-summary: How many keys were omitted past the cap.
keys_dropped_count.x-epack-method: Counts the keys removed from the key list past the 5,000 cap.

SecretsManagerMetrics.description: Secrets Manager metadata only. Secret VALUES are never collected.

secret_count.x-epack-summary: Secrets Manager secrets across the scanned regions.
secret_count.x-epack-method: Counts the secrets that ListSecrets returns in each scanned region with IncludePlannedDeletion set, so secrets scheduled for deletion count too.

secrets_without_rotation_count.x-epack-summary: Secrets with automatic rotation off. A leaked secret stays valid until someone changes it.
secrets_without_rotation_count.x-epack-method: Counts the secrets whose ListSecrets entry has RotationEnabled false or unset.

secrets_without_customer_kms_count.description: Secrets encrypted with the AWS managed key rather than a customer managed one.
secrets_without_customer_kms_count.x-epack-summary: Secrets encrypted with the AWS managed key for Secrets Manager. The account cannot edit that key's policy to limit who can decrypt them.
secrets_without_customer_kms_count.x-epack-method: Counts the secrets whose ListSecrets entry has no KmsKeyId.

secrets_pending_deletion_count.x-epack-summary: Secrets scheduled for deletion. A secret can be restored until its recovery window ends.
secrets_pending_deletion_count.x-epack-method: Counts the secrets whose ListSecrets entry has a DeletedDate. ListSecrets returns them because the request sets IncludePlannedDeletion.

secrets.description: Audit level and above: one row per secret, up to 5,000. Past the cap, the most recently changed are kept.
secrets.x-epack-summary: One metadata row per secret, capped at 5,000 with the most recently changed kept. Secret values are not collected.

secrets_truncated.description: Whether the secret list was cut at 5,000.
secrets_truncated.x-epack-summary: Whether the secret list was cut off at the cap.
secrets_truncated.x-epack-method: Records whether the combined secret list across regions had more than 5,000 secrets and was cut.

secrets_dropped_count.description: Secrets left out past the cap.
secrets_dropped_count.x-epack-summary: How many secrets were omitted past the cap.
secrets_dropped_count.x-epack-method: Counts the secrets removed from the secret list past the 5,000 cap.

SSMParametersMetrics.description: SSM Parameter Store metadata only. Parameter VALUES are never collected.

parameter_count.x-epack-summary: Parameter Store parameters across the scanned regions.
parameter_count.x-epack-method: Counts the parameters that DescribeParameters returns in each scanned region.

secure_string_count.description: SecureString parameters, the ones stored encrypted.
secure_string_count.x-epack-summary: Parameters stored as SecureString, which are encrypted at rest. String and StringList parameters are not encrypted with a KMS key.
secure_string_count.x-epack-method: Counts the parameters whose DescribeParameters Type is SecureString.

secure_strings_without_customer_kms_coun.description: SecureString parameters encrypted with the AWS managed key rather than a customer managed one.
secure_strings_without_customer_kms_coun.x-epack-summary: SecureString parameters encrypted with the AWS managed key for Parameter Store. The account cannot edit that key's policy to limit who can decrypt them.
secure_strings_without_customer_kms_coun.x-epack-method: Counts the SecureString parameters whose DescribeParameters KeyId is empty or starts with alias/aws/.

parameters.description: Audit level and above: one row per parameter, up to 10,000. Past the cap, the most recently changed are kept.
parameters.x-epack-summary: One metadata row per parameter, capped at 10,000 with the most recently changed kept. Parameter values are not collected.

parameters_truncated.description: Whether the parameter list was cut at 10,000.
parameters_truncated.x-epack-summary: Whether the parameter list was cut off at the cap.
parameters_truncated.x-epack-method: Records whether the combined parameter list across regions had more than 10,000 parameters and was cut.

parameters_dropped_count.description: Parameters left out past the cap.

web_acls.x-epack-summary: One row per web ACL, up to 1,000, with those attached to the most resources first.
